events.title: Mentor Session: Sean Herrity (US Trade Consult LLC)
events.description: Meeting with this mentor is highly recommended if you're interested in Business Development, Entrepreneurship, Food/AgTech, Funding, Sports, MedTech.

events.title: A Model for Culturally Responsive STEAM Ecosystems
events.description: How can gaming unlock access to STEAM careers for underrepresented youth? This panel explores the story of STEAM in Alexandria, VA, and a proven model that blends culturally responsive teaching, bilingual support, SEL, and industry exposure to create belonging. Participants will learn our scalable framework for building culturally responsive STEAM ecosystems through partnerships with higher ed, industry, and gaming partners. The session will also explore research-based strategies using gaming, project-based learning, and cultural content to build belonging in historically excluded students.

speakers.name: Chris Melissinos
speakers.title: Principal Evangelist, Video Games & Immersive Technologies

speakers.name: Kirk Knutsen
speakers.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant, Professionalism in Computing

events.title: PanelPicker & More: Engaging at SXSW EDU 2027 Meet Up
events.description: As SXSW EDU comes to an end, we are already prepping for 2027! Want to speak on the program or participate at the event? Stop by for information and tips, and learn about the many ways to get involved at next year’s event.

events.title: Rethinking Higher Education to Build an AI-First Workforce
events.description: AI's rapid integration risks leaving entire groups—and vast talent pools—behind. In this panel, explore the awareness gaps impacting low-income communities and actionable strategies to cultivate an inclusive, future-ready workforce. Learn how collaborations between today’s leading companies, nonprofits, and colleges/universities will prepare students for AI-driven careers. Ask important questions like, “should degrees even be required?,” hear real-world examples of employer-backed training to equip students with applied skills, and discover how initiatives like these can be replicated.

speakers.name: Evan Silberman
speakers.title: Interim Senior University Dean Of Academic Innovation, Chief Academic Technology Officer (Cato), & Office Of Academic Affairs

events.title: Thrive or Survive: Why Creativity is the Key to an AI-Future
events.description: AI may make life easier, but at what cost to our imagination? Like a bike we stop riding, our creativity weakens when we overrely on AI. Still, while adults may feel rusty, we can get back on. For children, the risk is even greater: if they never build that muscle in the first place—never learn to ride at all—there’s nothing to return to. This all comes just as jobs are being disrupted, problems grow more complex, and we need more imagination, not less. This panel explores how we can grow creatively with AI (versus be diminished by it) and what we must build now to make that future possible.

speakers.name: Andrea Virgin
speakers.title: Chair & CEO
speakers.company: The Center for Arts & Innovation, Inc.

events.title: Workforce Innovation in Production & the Creative Economy
events.description: How can we reimagine training and workforce development in film, media, and the creative industries as technology, production models, and industry needs rapidly evolve? This meetup convenes educators, workforce leaders, and entertainment professionals to explore innovative approaches for preparing set-ready talent and upskilling current professionals. Participants will share strategies, examine gaps, and discuss how policy levers like film tax credits, emerging technology, and cross-sector collaboration can create scalable, equitable pathways from education to sustainable careers.

events.title: The Art Gallery is the New Gym: Get Creative, Get Smarter
events.description: Engaging art is a creative act. There are art galleries and museums everywhere. Let's use them well. Art objects aren't puzzles to solve, but rather invitations to experience something new and make it personally meaningful. As Josiah McElheny explains, “The experience of art is a kind of fusion of your experience of yourself and of the object.” In doing this personal creativity is exercised and you get smarter. This session will get you started on doing it well, showing how to exercise effectively.

events.title: Burger Mart From Invincible, Brought to You by Brisk
events.description: Step into your own episode of Invincible at the show’s iconic Burger Mart, built from the ground up in collaboration with Brisk. Order a hot BM and fries, get your photo taken at the scenic center booth, score a free custom Brisk can, and walk away with a full swag bag of exclusive merch.

events.title: EdTech Product Development in an AI Powered World
events.description: The Entrepreneur in Residence and Director of Innovative Programs at Catalyst @ Penn GSE will share insights on what founders can do to position their start-up for success in a post-pandemic and AI-powered world. John will present the current investment climate, trends in AI and machine learning, and a research-based model for attracting investors and scaling their venture for long-term competitive advantage.

speakers.name: John Gamba
speakers.title: Entrepreneur in Residence
speakers.company: University of Pennsylvania's Graduate School of Education

events.title: The F-Stop
events.description: The F-Stop is bringing Focus Features films Obsession and The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist to life through an immersive traveling Airstream experience. Step inside for immersive visuals, exclusive merch, and a creative breather between screenings, all inspired by bold, auteur‑driven storytelling.

events.title: Invincible VS Arcade Pop Up
events.description: Invincible VS, a new 3x3 tag fighter launching on April 30, 2026, is appearing at SXSW with an exclusive arcade pop up featuring a roster of 10 playable characters including a new unannounced fan favorite fighter. Free swag and giveaways will be available for all who come to play the most epic and bloody fight in the universe, with a special gift for fans who pre-order the game onsite or show proof of preorder.

events.title: Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man - The Garrison
events.description: The Garrison at SXSW is an immersive experience that transports guests into the world of Netflix's film Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man. Rich in period detail, the space channels the grit and glamour of the Shelby legacy through a custom bar, beer taps, whiskey-forward cocktails, and vintage seating. Included are hidden “easter eggs”, allowing fans to step inside the story, stay a while, and leave with a Peaky-inspired tattoo or trim as a lasting memory.

events.title: SXSW Film & TV Clubhouse
events.description: The Film & TV Clubhouse is located at 800 Congress Ave, just steps away from the Paramount Theatre, where some of the most exciting screenings of the Festival are set to premiere. It will serve as the home base for the film community to gather, discuss, and network. Each day the Film & TV Clubhouse will host meetups and networking events as well as activations.

events.title: SXSW Innovation Clubhouse
events.description: The historic Brazos Hall is the official Innovation Clubhouse for 2026. It's the perfect place to connect with attendees looking to gain insights and inspiration from like-minded conference-goers. Each day the Innovation Clubhouse will host meetups and networking events as well as activations.

events.title: Vibrating Music Hammocks
events.description:
The Music Hammock transforms its fabric into a speaker, resonating your body with the frequencies of the music so you feel as if you’re lying inside a sound system. In our fast-paced society, we often disconnect from our bodies. This installation offers a full-body listening experience, shifting your attention from mental chatter into physical awareness. Experience sound not only through your ears, but through your entire body.

https://www.parkerhertzberger.nl/portfolio-collections/my-portfolio/project-title-6

The Music Hammock transforms its fabric into a speaker, resonating your body with the frequencies of the music so you feel as if you’re lying inside a sound system. Experience sound not only through your ears, but through your entire body.

events.title: Keynote: Jennifer B Wallace
events.description: Bestselling author Jennifer Wallace explores mattering — the human need to feel valued and add value — as the secret ingredient to lifelong wellbeing and the key to deep connections and purpose. Drawing on global research and powerful stories, she reveals how mattering offers a potent antidote to loneliness and burnout, and delivers practical takeaways to help people unlock mattering at home, at work, and in the wider world.

events.title: Redbreast Unhidden Box Office
events.description:
The Redbreast Unhidden Box Office lands in Austin this SXSW, from March 12–14 on Congress Avenue, across from the iconic Paramount Theatre, celebrating exceptional Irish whiskey and cinema. Collect your ticket from our Redbreast concierges for an exclusive Redbreast Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey tasting and enjoy the chance to win prizes.

Attendees must be over 21. On-site registration required.

events.title: Japan Meetup in cooperation with JTB
events.description: Coffee, culture, and connection! Head to the Japan Pavilion at the International Innovation Expo for a unique networking mixer.  This is your chance to meet Japan’s most creative exhibitors and connect with Japanese attendees over a cup of coffee. Everyone is welcome — don’t miss the chance to spark new ideas and new friendships!

events.title: From Burnout to Bandwidth: Using AI to Reclaim Your Day
events.description: Drowning in emails, planning, paperwork, and those boring (but necessary) administrative tasks? In this hands-on session, discover practical AI tools that automate routine tasks, generate content, analyze data, and simplify communication, freeing you to focus on students and strategy. Leave with real-world examples, ready-to-use ideas, and strategies to reduce burnout, improve efficiency, and reignite your creativity. Learn how AI can help you save time on low-level tasks so you can focus on the high-level tasks that bring maximum impact to your job.

events.title: From Insight to Impact: Superintendents Share What Works
events.description: Want to understand how superintendents make purchasing decisions? Join leaders from the Institute for Education Innovation (IEI), a national superintendent think tank committed to fostering meaningful partnerships between districts and ed tech innovators. IEI superintendents will share candid insights and firsthand experiences to help founders and executives design solutions that truly support student success. The conversation will be guided by a superintendent emeritus and a 20-year industry veteran who has helped hundreds of ed tech companies grow and scale effectively.

events.title: In Search of Hope: Teaching Climate Emotions Through Story
events.description: Climate change impacts students not just physically, but emotionally as well. This session introduces the H.O.P.E. Framework (Healing Opportunities for Processing Eco-Grief), a practical, story-based approach for helping teachers and students recognize and respond to climate emotions. Rooted in hope theory and literature, the framework offers tools to spark meaningful conversations and build emotional resilience. Participants will explore current research, hear from educators using the approach, and leave with ready-to-use resources for emotionally responsive climate education.

speakers.name: Colleen Redmond
speakers.title: PhD Student, Graduate Instructor, Research Assistant in Literacy Education, & Co-Founder paleBLUEdot

events.title: Steal C-Suite Tools to Reset Schools, Like a Boss
events.description: This session challenges the school culture status quo by showing how educators can borrow the proven systems, tools, and communication practices that power high-performing workplaces. We’ll unpack how school teams can move from burnout and dysfunction to clarity and cohesion—using corporate strategies that work. It’s not about turning schools into businesses—it’s about building better environments for people who care.

events.title: Jennifer B. Wallace Book Signing
events.description: Jennifer B. Wallace will be signing copies of “Mattering: The Secret to a Life of Deep Connection and Purpose” at the SXSW Bookstore.

events.title: The Big Blur: Rethinking the Transition from School to Work
events.description: What if high school, college, and career weren’t separate systems—but one seamless experience designed to help today’s learners succeed in a fast-changing world of work? This panel explores “The Big Blur,” a bold vision to redesign how we educate 16–20-year-olds by erasing the boundaries between K–12, higher education, and work. Panelists will share how they’re building learning models that integrate academics, career-connected learning, and real credentials—starting in high school. Hear how these efforts are creating real opportunity for students and what it will take to scale nationwide.

events.title: Brazil Creative Economy Meet Up
events.description: Brazil has one of the most innovative creative economies in the world. It is influenced by its multicultural background, versatility and diversity that shape and inspire its creative economy ecosystem. Come meet some of Brazil's communication professionals, audio-visual producers, designers, publishers, brands and startups, where a fluid exchange of ideas, business models and collaborations will take place. This is a place of encounter to develop a mutual and beneficial culture of exchange between all SXSW attendees and the Brazilian creative community.

events.title: Chalk & Gavel: Navigating the Tides of an Education Law Sea Change
events.description: In this live recording of Chalk & Gavel, education law professors Drs. Jamie Kudlats and Chris Thomas will explore the current legal landscape reshaping K–12 schools—from book bans and parental opt-out policies to religious liberty disputes and protecting our most vulnerable students. Jamie, a former middle school math teacher and principal, and Chris, a former English teacher and school attorney, will break down major legal shifts, key issues, and share insights to empower educators and advocates to navigate an evolving legal and political landscape.

speakers.name: Jamie Kudlats
speakers.title: Assistant Professor of Educational Leadership
speakers.company: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

speakers.name: Christopher Thomas
speakers.title: Assistant Professor of Educational Leadership and Policy

events.title: Charmageddon: Robots That Steal Hearts and Jobs
events.description:
Robots are no longer confined to factories. Today, they work in offices, live in homes, and support people in hospitals. But even the most advanced technical performance doesn’t ensure success. What often makes the difference? Likeability.

In this talk, we explore how product strategy, design and character development help robots go from impressive machines to trusted companions. Through real-world case studies, we’ll show how emotional connection can be just as important as capability.

events.title: The Education Founders Meet Up at SXSW EDU
events.description:
Calling all education founders!

If you’re building a company that serves schools, districts, or higher ed — especially in this fast-moving era of AI — this room is for you. Join us for an energizing hour of real connection with fellow education founders who understand the unique challenges of building, selling , and scaling in this market.

We’ll kick off with a fast-paced session and create space for conversations about growth, funding, AI integration, and long sales cycles.

Come find your next collaborator, mentor, or strategic partner — and leave with clarity, momentum, and community.

speakers.name: John Gamba
speakers.title: Entrepreneur in Residence
speakers.company: University of Pennsylvania's Graduate School of Education

events.title: Exploring the Future of Space and Japan's Deep-Tech
events.description: Japan is rapidly emerging as a bold new force in space mobility. This session brings together Woven Capital, Innovative Space Carrier, Sora Material, and Deloitte to reveal how Japan’s deep-tech breakthroughs—reusable launch systems, orbital transportation architectures, and ultra-light materials that almost float in air—are reshaping the future of Earth-to-Orbit-to-Moon mobility. From Toyota’s global investment strategy to Japan’s first private U.S. VTVL launch, the speakers will share frontier insights and new opportunities for global collaboration with Japan’s rising space industry.

speakers.name: Will Rice
speakers.title: Strategy Director and Chief of Staff

speakers.name: Nanako Hirano
speakers.title: Senior Consultant
speakers.company: Deloitte Tohmatsu Venture Support Co., Ltd.

events.title: Featured Session: How to Support Resilient Youth in an AI World
events.description:
Generative AI is rapidly reshaping how young people learn, connect, and understand themselves. From AI tutors and creative tools to always-on digital companions, these technologies promise new opportunities, but also raise urgent questions about children’s cognitive, social, and emotional development. Rather than focusing on whether AI should be used in education, how do we ensure AI strengthens—rather than undermines—young people’s capacity to think, relate, and thrive?

Drawing from the recent Brookings report "A New Direction for Students in an AI World: Prosper, Prepare, Protect,” with data across 50 countries, this panel will include a rich mix of perspectives and explore what it truly means to support resilient youth in an AI-saturated world.

events.title: Future-Ready Frameworks for Higher Ed's Title IX Challenges
events.description: Our panel of experienced lawyers brings different perspectives to the evolving Title IX legal landscape. We are student advocates, policy designers, and on-the-ground implementers. We will share strategies for transforming Title IX challenges into opportunities and explore how forward-thinking institutions can move from reactive approaches toward sustainable, sound policies and fair processes that serve all students. Through case studies and practical frameworks, participants will learn strategies for balancing legal requirements with institutional values in the classroom and beyond.

events.title: Glowing Brains & Robosuits: Terminating the AI Cliché
events.description:
The metaphors we use shape the futures we create. While the whole world becomes human-AI hybrid, we still talk about AI like a god, ghost or omnipotent spreadsheet.
Corporate ‘cyborg-centaur’ sci-fi clichés trap organisations in macho, mechanistic tropes. We urgently need new myths to think with. Bring your sledgehammer as we deconstruct the lazy visual language of AI. Whether you’re designing tech, making art or building teams, the models unveiled in this session will give you the tools you need to take control and make AI an effective, equitable partner in the redesign of the new workplace.

speakers.name: Jacqueline O'Reilly
speakers.title: Professor at the University of Sussex Business School & Co-Director of the ESRC Digital Futures at Work Research Centre (Digit)

events.title: Higher Ed's Losing Global Talent & the Bill Is Coming Due
events.description: International students drive innovation, fill urgent workforce gaps and contributed more than $45B to the U.S. economy last year, yet global demand for U.S. study is slipping fast. This session dives into why enrollment is declining and what institutions must do now to compete. Expect sharp insights on shifting student expectations, career-aligned pathways, smarter English-language readiness, affordability pressures and the policies shaping where talent goes next. A must-attend for anyone rethinking international recruitment and preparing for the next era of global mobility.

events.title: Let’s Talk Spanglish
events.description: Meet up with Spanish- and English-speaking peers to practice bilingualism in a welcoming, judgment-free space designed for educators. Participants will explore the power of linguistic diversity in learning environments, experience a low-stakes card-based activity that fosters authentic language use, and reflect on how social interaction supports language development. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to build inclusive, multilingual classrooms and communities.

events.title: LGBTQ+ & Friends Meet Up
events.description: This is a space to pause, breathe, and connect. We bring bubbles for your inner child, stories that spark connection, and space to show up exactly as you are. Join LGBTQ+, friends, creatives and  storytellers, for an authentic gathering rooted in curiosity, community, and queer joy. Come curious, leave connected. We can honestly say that for 4 years that we've done it for SXSW, this is the space where we had made the most unique and stronger connections!

events.title: The Lie That You’re Not Creative
events.description: Creativity is no longer a “nice to have.” As technology takes over efficiency and execution, creativity has become the essential human skill – fueling clarity, adaptability, and connection in times of rapid change. This session reframes creativity not as talent, but as a core capability anyone can access. Through practical tools and real-world examples, participants will learn how creativity helps us navigate uncertainty, think more flexibly, and stay grounded, resilient, and human in an increasingly automated world.

events.title: Mall Rats Reborn: How Hot Topic is Using Entertainment to Revitalise Retail
events.description: Malls may be losing commercial relevance, but some brands are reclaiming their cultural relevance. In a widely successful experimental pilot, Hot Topic has launched two social-first sitcoms shot entirely in malls, casting creators from punk, goth, and cosplay scenes to reclaim its ALT roots. As Gen Z flocks back to IRL hangouts and “third places,” the brand is transforming shopping centres into entertainment stages. It’s part of a wider shift toward entertainment-first marketing, echoing moves by brands like Dick’s Sporting Goods, which have built in-house studios to power the growth of their own and partner brands. Hear from Hot Topic and their agency partners Small W•rld about how to pull this strategy off successfully.

events.title: Mentor Session: Gary Forni (Central Texas Angel Network)

events.title: Pedagogy, Politics, & Place: Video PD for a Polarized Age
events.description: With the 250th anniversary of the United States nearing, the need for accurate, engaging, and factual instruction has never been more urgent. Educators need professional development that is both flexible and trustworthy. Museums and nonprofits - longstanding partners in education - are responding to this moment by reimagining professional learning through video-based formats that preserve the power of place and story. This panel explores how these organizations are using video to support educators in navigating today’s polarized educational landscape with clarity, confidence and integrity.

events.title: Reigniting STEM Interest: A 7,700-Student Study
events.description: In an era of global challenges—from clean water to AI ethics—we need an avalanche of young innovators, yet STEM interest drops during the middle-to-high school transition. A 7,700-student study reveals 6 levers that raise engagement: meaningful experiences, parent influence, unlocking girls’ participation, courage/agency, clear career images, and reframing difficulty. Take away a shared language, tested patterns, and next steps for applying them through Activation → Identity → Career.

events.title: The Story of Stories—The Million Year History of Storytelling
events.description: "Language did not give us stories; stories gave us language." Kevin Ashton coined the phrase "the Internet of Things" and led the development of the Internet of Things at MIT. His latest book THE STORY OF STORIES explores the intrinsic human nature of storytelling; delves into how stories are deeply embedded in our lives; and traces the evolution of storytelling from night fires to digital screens, social media, AI, and beyond. Kevin will read from the book, discuss its big ideas, take questions, and, after the talk, sign books at the SXSW bookstore.

events.title: Unleashing Students' Tech Genius to Improve Mental Health
events.description: Panelists will discuss emerging tech-driven mental health solutions and the importance of involving end users – in this case, college students – in their development. Centered on the student-led creation of a first-of-its-kind AI tool to support mental health, this discussion with the project’s researchers and students will emphasize the need to let research guide how we integrate AI into healthcare to harness its benefits without creating new harms, all while empowering students to become ethical stewards of AI.

speakers.name: Lisa Marsch
speakers.title: Director, Center for Technology and Behavioral Health

events.title: Your Attention Please
events.description:
A new generation of parents, teens, and reformers are fighting back against Big Tech’s agenda to define the future of human connection. From Kristin, a mother pursuing legislative reform after losing her son, to Trisha, a young programmer building technology to stop cyberbullying, the film reveals how deeply the attention economy is reshaping us.

Blending intimate human stories with insights from leading experts in tech reform and digital wellbeing, "Your Attention Please" asks some of the most urgent questions of our time: Can we reclaim our autonomy? Can technology be redesigned to serve humanity? And what does a healthier relationship with the digital world look like for us and our kids?

events.title: American Doctor
events.description: American Doctor is a vérité non-fiction film following three prominent physicians–Palestinian, Jewish and Zoroastrian—friends who couldn’t be more different but are bound by the shared oath to heal. Dr. Thaer Ahmad is measured, Dr. Mark Perlmutter is blunt, and Dr. Feroze Sidhwa is steeped in scholarship. Filmed in unfolding, on-the-ground scenes, the story follows them from a Gazan hospital under siege, to the halls of Congress. Together they fight to keep a promise to their Palestinian colleagues and patients, which is to continue the struggle where it matters most: the United States.

events.title: Agridulce (Bittersweet)
events.description:
In the Dominican town of Cabarete, bachata is a way of life far from the dance halls that it occupies overseas. A snapshot of four children, each confronting an existential challenge, Agridulce shows how music guides their journey of self discovery. With five years of filming, director Frank Pavich (Jodorowsky’s Dune) captures pivotal moments of the children’s coming of age.

Generations collide, and the children struggle for balance in a world troubled by conflict. Along the way, they’re mentored by teachers of a school devoted to bachata, the once denigrated music that has become the Dominican Republic’s primary cultural export.

events.title: Anima
events.description: After being let go from her robotic companion start-up, Beck, an anti-social engineer, finds herself in the offices of a new company claiming to preserve a person's consciousness inside a cloud system. Her first assignment: drive the company's most valuable client, Paul, a lonely button manufacturer, to his final appointment.

events.title: Dead Eyes
events.description: A firest person horror film. Sean and his fiancée, Grace, enter a remote forest to find Sean’s missing father, Paul, who vanished after the death of his youngest daughter, Lilly. Returning to the site of Lilly’s death forces Sean to confront his inner demons, which begin to materialize externally. Their search takes a terrifying turn, revealing Paul’s secret. He’s been conducting experiments, aimed at resurrecting Lilly. The forest is now inhabited by cannibalistic little girls, each a clone of Lilly, battling to prove their identity as the 'real' Lilly. As Sean and Grace uncover the grim truth, they face terrifying creatures and grapple with unsettling questions about life and death.

events.title: Mile End Kicks
events.description: Grace Pine, a driven though easily distracted 23-year-old. She leaves her quirky parents’ home for a shared apartment found on Craigslist to devote herself to writing the next great book in the 33 1/3 album exploration series. Hers will be on the iconic Alanis Morissette opus Jagged Little Pill. Loft parties introduce Grace to two paramours. Unfortunately, they are members of the same rock band, Bone Patrol. And instead of sequestering herself away to complete her draft, she uses her music industry know-how to get in with the band as their publicist.Through wine-fuelled poetry readings and other ill-advised choices, Grace is in the trenches of self-discovery.

events.title: Reducing the Cognitive Cost of Change to Drive Innovation
events.description:
Change keeps coming fast. Teams, educators, and leaders are being asked to adopt new tools, behaviors, and priorities at a relentless pace. But many change efforts fail to stick. People feel overwhelmed, disconnected, or left behind. Change does not fail because people resist it. It fails because of how we design and deliver it.
This session rethinks change through the lens of learning science. Drawing on research around metacognition, motivation, and cognitive load, we’ll explore why transformation stalls when people can’t see the relevance, can’t experiment safely, or simply can’t keep up.

events.title: Startup Lessons from the Baby-Sitters Club
events.description: The Baby-Sitters Club was a female-founded startup that thrived in the care economy, which included early-childhood education. This session highlights how the startup founders responded to local demand, built trust, and scaled their service with limited resources. Their fee-for-service business model provided affordable childcare to families. The Baby-Sitters Club incorporated empathy, social and emotional learning, creativity, and collaborative leadership into their core values. These business practices and values are transferable to startups in the real and modern world.

events.title: Texas High School Shorts Screening & Q&A
events.description: Please join us in welcoming the Texas High School Shorts to the SXSW EDU Film Program! This block of screenings will feature thirteen short films: “Just ask.” -- A boy fixates over asking a girl out at a subway station after recently being rejected.“The Cookie Quest” -- A young baker contracts an illness that stops her from being able to do what she loves. She struggles with her symptoms, eventually baking one cookie, beginning the transition back to her normal life.“Lyle in Love” -- Lyle must choose whether or not to ask out the girl whom he cherishes most.“Eclipse” -- The Sun is passing by the Moon. Remember to wear your sunglasses.“Wendigo” -- A lonely shapeshifter tries to make friends in a big forest.“She Follows Me” -- “She Follows Me” introduces Harper, a teenage girl struggling with depression who is contemplating suicide, until an unexpected visitor helps her rediscover a part of her life that she thought was gone forever.“Uno” -- When Derian cheats in a friendly game of Uno, his friend seeks revenge with the help of a magical Uno card. “Bear Bones” -- Bear Bones follows the surreal journey of a teddy bear.“DASH’D” -- A regular dude can't decide what to order on a food delivery app.“Operation Goliath” -- Two soldiers, Pat and Hank, are trapped behind enemy lines in a dense jungle, but a new threat is waiting in the darkness.“New Heights – with JD Wallace – New Heights follows Joshua” -- “JD” Wallace, a 6’5” Jack Yates High School senior whose rise as a student-athlete challenges every assumption about him—revealing that true elevation isn’t just about height, but speed, precision, discipline, and purpose.“Hot Off the Reel - with Ken Burns” -- As Jack Yates High School approaches its 100-year anniversary, four JY Cinema Dual Credit students step into the world of professional documentary filmmaking when they meet legendary filmmaker Ken Burns at Houston PBS. “Gambini Fights Lucheesy (TONY???) and the Lucheeses: The Movie” -- Two omnipotent mafia bosses engage in a fierce battle for the perfect croissant recipe.Following the final film, there will be a Q&A with the audience featuring the student filmmakers.

events.title: Baby/Girls
events.description: In post-Dobbs rural Arkansas, teen birth rates remain among the highest in the nation, shaped by generational patterns and limited access to sex education. For pregnant teenagers with limited family support, a Christian maternity home provides housing, prenatal care, and faith-based guidance. Filmed over two years with intimate verité access, Baby/Girls remains inside the house as three young women move through pregnancy, give birth, and step into motherhood. They come from families marked by poverty, addiction, and abuse; several are daughters of teen mothers themselves, continuing cycles that span generations. The film offers a powerful portrait of lives we often cannot see.

events.description: Vibrant work filmed in, inspired by, or connected to the Lone Star State.
events.venue: Rollins Theatre at the Long Center

events.title: Perfect
events.description: In a world devastated by a contaminated water supply, Kai, a lost soul, finds herself living out of her car after a bad breakup. Each day is a struggle until fate intervenes and leads her to a hidden utopian lake, where the water is pure and life flourishes. At this secret haven, Kai encounters a band of eccentric misfits each with their own stories of loss and hope. Among them is Mallory, an enigmatic and wealthy pregnant woman living out an escapist fantasy. Despite their vastly different backgrounds, Kai and Mallory are drawn to each other, and a sudden, passionate romance ignites. As their bond deepens, Kai begins to uncover the layers of Mallory’s life and the secrets she harbors.

events.title: Capturing Bigfoot
events.description:
On October 20, 1967, Roger Patterson captured 59 seconds of film showing a creature walking through the Northern California woods—footage that became the most analyzed and debated in history. Fifty-seven years later, a reel of 16mm film discovered in a safe changes everything.

"Capturing Bigfoot" reveals the untold story behind the world's greatest mystery, told for the first time by Patterson's own son and the people who were there.

This is a story about family legacy, broken friendships, and belief itself.

events.title: Dead Deer High
events.description:
DEAD DEER HIGH follows a team of high school slam poets and their English teacher as they prepare for a national poetry competition one year after a tragedy changed their lives forever.

A powerful story of healing, poetry, and resilience in the face of tragedy, Dead Deer High was directed, written, produced, and edited by teachers.

events.title: AI with Aloha: Stories from Hawai‘i’s Classrooms
events.description: While most schools banned AI when it first emerged, one school in Hawai‘i saw the wave coming and started paddling early. As the emerging technology teacher at ‘Iolani School, my goal was to make every mistake as quickly as possible so that we can learn valuable lessons together. We knew from day one that AI was here to stay, so while others watched from shore, my students and I were wiping out, experimenting, and figuring it out together. This session shares the stories from those chaotic early days and how they led to the AI literacy programs we’ve built in Hawai‘i today.

events.title: Asian Creator Economy Meet Up
events.description: Since 2023, the Asian Creator Economy Meet Up has created space for Asian creators, professionals in the creator economy, and allies to gather, connect, and grow. As the industry evolves, so does our need for culturally grounded, forward-looking conversations. From monetization and visibility to community care and platform shifts, this space invites creators to share what’s working, what’s changing, and how we can thrive together. Our goal is to hold space where identity and innovation meet.

events.title: Augmented Reality & Place-Based Learning: Layers of Place
events.description: This interactive workshop explores how augmented reality (AR) can be used as a pedagogical tool to deepen learners’ relationships to place, memory, and community. Drawing from Layers of Place: Austin—a collection of six location-based AR artworks—participants will engage with artists’ approaches to place-based storytelling, public history, and experiential learning. Through discussion, short activities, and case studies, the session examines how AR can function as a method for cultivating attention, care, and critical engagement with the spaces we inhabit.

events.title: "Bathe in Beats" Official Wellness Social Kickoff Party At SXSW 2026
events.description:
Bathe in Beats is an official SXSW Kickoff Wellness Social that blends music, nervous system optimization, art, and social connection into a half-day immersive experience that reflects the true pulse of Austin culture today.

As SXSW opens the city to creators, innovators, and cultural leaders from around the world, Bathe in Beats offers a radically different entry point into the week: not another party that burns people out, but a somatic, sensory, and social reset that fuels creativity, connection, and longevity.

This experience showcases how music, wellness, and culture are no longer separate worlds, they are colliding, collaborating, and reshaping how people gather.

events.title: Beyond Borders: Diverse Alliances for Immigrant Wellbeing
events.description: Immigrant children and families face rising stress often missed by traditional systems. This session explores cross-sector (public, private, nonprofit) and cross-disciplinary (health, education, TV, community organizing) collaboration to foster innovative, community-rooted solutions. Participants will engage in hands-on, small-group case studies centered on real-world challenges facing immigrant children and families, gaining practical experience applying cross-sector strategies to complex issues.

events.title: Beyond Voting: Defending Truth in Education: AI, Equity, & Power
events.description: Join Beyond Voting for a live conversation exposing how AI fuels authoritarianism in education—erasing marginalized scholarship, surveilling students, and exploiting hidden labor. We’ll examine threats to academic freedom, student privacy, and the educator workforce, and highlight how educators and students—especially those from marginalized communities—can fight for equity, protect dissent, and defend truth in learning and research.

events.title: Building AI Pathways for HBCU Talent & Community Impact
events.description: As AI rapidly reshapes education and work, HBCUs sit at a critical intersection of talent development, cultural stewardship, and community accountability. This panel brings together higher education, industry, and ecosystem leaders to examine how ethical AI pathways can be built with HBCUs—not around them. Panelists will explore practical models for aligning curriculum, workforce pipelines, industry partnerships, and community impact so AI innovation leads to access, ownership, and long-term opportunity for Black talent and communities.

events.title: Culture Under Fire: Storytelling for Public Power
events.description: Public libraries, theaters, and arts institutions face growing threats from budget cuts, censorship, and consolidation—but remain vital to civic life. This panel unites the Future Film Coalition (FFC), American Library Association  (ALA), and Americans for the Arts (AFTA) to share concrete strategies for defending public cultural infrastructure. From local advocacy to national coalition-building, panelists will offer tools to help artists and communities protect access, uphold free expression, and strengthen an equitable media ecosystem.

speakers.name: Lisa Varga
speakers.title: Associate Executive Director, Public Policy And Advocacy

events.title: Featured Session: Social Health Trends & Predictions: Connection is the New Frontier
events.description: Social health is today where mental health was 10-15 years ago—but we’ve reached a turning point. That was the bold claim from leading expert Kasley Killam in her SXSW 2025 opening keynote. This year, she’s back to reveal the most important breakthroughs, trends, and predictions shaping the rapidly growing movement to transform society through connection and community. Drawing on new research and cutting-edge innovation around the globe, Killam will surface surprising insights, the most promising opportunities for impact, and an inspiring vision of what’s next. No matter your industry, this is the session you can’t miss if you want to understand—and help lead—the future of relationships, longevity, and human thriving.

speakers.name: Kasley Killam
speakers.title: Author
speakers.company: The Art and Science of Connection

events.title: The Future is Low-Tech: Lessons from the Early 2000s
events.description:
Let's rewind back to the early 2000s – slower interfaces, finite gameplay, loading bars, shared family computers and digital experiences that rewarded patience, curiosity and real-world interaction.

In this talk, we'll unpack the overlooked design features of the era and explore how they can be applied today.

This session is for designers, educators, technologists and decision-makers who want to take part in building a low-tech future!

speakers.name: Jésabel DC
speakers.title: Low-Tech Futurist | Tech Anthropologist | EdTech Founder

events.title: Future Tense: A Vibecoding Experience for Educators
events.description: After 3+ years of AI panels and predictions, most people still haven't experienced the technology in a way that makes the stakes visceral. This hands-on workshop changes that. Participants will "vibe code"—building functional software through conversation with AI, no technical background required. You'll create your first learning tool in 10 minutes, iterate with peers, and leave with a working prototype. We'll close by exploring what this means for the future of learning and the future of work: What happens when anyone can build software? What skills matter when routine tasks get automated? Less philosophizing, more co-creating.

events.title: Higher Ed Needs Caring & Liberatory Leadership to Thrive
events.description: This fireside chat will include a discussion of two new approaches that challenge status quo organization and leadership practices in higher education. Namely, staff, faculty, and leaders are invited to engage in systemic and structural changes aligned with liberation praxis and the ethics of care. Drawing from organizational theories, the social sciences, research, and lived experience, the discussants will challenge each other and the audience to imagine the personal and institutional changes required to promote employee well-being and creativity in today’s higher education workplace.

events.title: How To Meaningfully Connect in a World That Has Gone to Sh*t
events.description:
We live in the most “connected” era in human history — and yet loneliness, burnout, and distrust are at historic highs. Convenience has replaced care. Algorithms now mediate our relationships. And many of us have quietly lost our ability to sit with difference, discomfort, and each other.

In this deeply human, and surprisingly hopeful keynote, McPherson explores how technology and current political strife have weakened our connection muscle, and why empathy and intentional friction are the missing ingredients in rebuilding trust, collaboration, and belonging. Drawing on two decades of work across corporations, nonprofits, and movements, Susan shares practical, actionable ways teams and leaders can foster genuine connection — online and in person — without adding more meetings, tools, or performative “culture” initiatives. This talk is a call to reconnect — not by opting out of technology, but by remembering how to be human with it.

events.title: How to Raise Changemakers: Lessons from Brazil’s Youth
events.description: What if we raised teens to lead change, not just pass tests? This session dives into practical ways educators and families can nurture empathy, leadership, and civic engagement in youth. Based on real experiences of Brazilian teens who became changemakers through a Youth Volunteer Project that connects them with social impact causes and community work, this panel will offer tested strategies to help students break social bubbles, build empathy, find purpose, and take action, inside and outside the classroom.

events.title: Human Futures: Learning in a Tech-Shaped World
events.description: Through open dialogue, participants will examine how emerging tools reshape learning environments and expand access to knowledge. The meetup invites attendees to interrogate the ways tech products and services are shaping education, challenge assumptions, and imagine new models of collaboration. Through our reporting, we cover how technology sparks more inclusive, creative, culturally relevant experiences outside the West.

events.title: It Takes a Region: Cybersecurity Pathways in Rural Alabama
events.description: In rural eastern Alabama, a cybersecurity talent pipeline is taking root—powered by bold collaboration between K–12 schools, postsecondary institutions, and local industry. This session shares how a regional alliance is designing hands-on learning experiences, embedding aligned credentials, and unlocking high-wage, high-demand careers for students. Discover how a rural community is transforming opportunity through workforce-aligned education and community-wide vision.

events.title: Paramount+ The Lodge
events.description: The Paramount+ Lodge returns with the ultimate fan experience, offering an unforgettable and immersive journey that lets guests engage with hit content, iconic franchises and live championship sports. Back for its fourth consecutive year, the Lodge takes over Clive Bar on Austin’s Rainey Street, transporting fans and new audiences into the worlds of their favorite series and sports on Paramount+.

events.title: Shaping Education in a Culture x Tech World
events.description: At the intersection of art and technology, education is shifting from instruction to experimentation. This interactive Meet Up focuses on non-linear, learner-driven approaches where technology acts as a creative collaborator—not a skill to master. Through facilitated discussion, we’ll examine how knowledge emerges when disciplines collide and learning grows from uncertainty rather than fixed structures.

speakers.name: Lori Baker
speakers.title: Executive Vice President for Global Strategy & Programs

events.title: Shortchanged: Gen Z, the Economy, and Brands
events.description: As economic opportunity slips further out of reach for young adults, brands face a new reality: a generation facing high living costs, stagnant wages, and declining opportunity is redefining how, why, and where they spend. This session explores how financial precarity is reshaping consumer behavior and what it means for marketers. Learn how to build relevance and win over a generation that’s not just broke, but breaking the mold.

events.title: Skills You’ll Need To Succeed in the Post-AI Age
events.description:
We’re living and working in the AI age.
But you already knew that.

The question is: What can you do to prepare, manage, and make the most of AI-inspired change?
This session is here to give you answers. It’s based on the Skills Horizon, a dynamic guide to everything you need to know next. And it features practical insights and wisdom drawn from conversations about tech, mindset, creativity, trust, productivity, and other big topics with dozens of leaders from around the world.

In just one hour, you’ll walk away ready to succeed and lead in these AI-centric times.

speakers.name: Kai Riemer
speakers.title: Professor and Director of Sydney Executive Plus

events.title: Cultural Conquest: The Digital Black American Blueprint
events.description: In the age of algorithms and automation, what does it mean to protect the essence of Black creativity? This session traces how the history of cultural appropriation is now mirrored through digital platforms, machine learning, and AI-generated content. Grammy-winning producer and strategist Shalom J. Storm Miller presents a future-facing blueprint for cultural integrity, offering educators, creatives, and technologists a framework for sustaining Black influence in an increasingly synthetic world.

events.title: Teaching for All with Less: Bold Moves in Inclusive Practice
events.description: Traditional differentiation is dead. Every child can grow—if given the chance. But too many neurodivergent students disengage when teachers lack the tools to adapt. With limited budgets and rising classroom complexity, we need a shift: inclusive education must become the standard, not the specialist’s job. This session challenges old models and showcases bold, realistic ways to embed adaptive teaching, reward innovation, and empower every educator—without asking for more time or money, just better thinking.

events.title: Crossover Day Mixer
events.description: Crossover Day is where the family of SXSW conferences and festivals converge. This networking event is an invitation for SXSW and SXSW EDU registrants to come together for a celebration of innovation in education and creativity. Join Imaginable Futures, presenter of the Crossover Day Mixer, to reimagine the stories we tell about learning in a moment when our relationships with technology—and with each other—are being rewritten.More information here: https://imaginablefutures.com/united-states/

events.title: DJ AG
events.description:
DJ AG is a genre-shifting DJ and producer whose influence sits at the crossroads of Black British culture, global pop and contemporary electronic music. His sets move from grime and UK rap to afrobeats and alternative soul without losing pace or purpose. This approach has made him a trusted name for artists and audiences who want more than a standard club experience.

AG has shared stages with and played for artists including Ed Sheeran, Will Smith, Burna Boy and Skepta. His profile continues to grow as he brings his sound to live shows, brand events and cultural moments that pull in diverse crowds. Known for reading a room with accuracy rather than hype, AG builds environments where every transition feels intentional.

His work has been covered by a range of platforms and press titles reflecting his reach across culture, style and music. Coverage includes features and appearances in GRM Daily, Complex, Notion, Trench, Mixtape Madness and BBC platforms which have positioned him as one of the most versatile names emerging from the UK scene.

events.title: Future in Focus: Meet Germany’s Top AI Startups
events.description:
Germany’s boldest AI innovators take the stage at SXSW, ready to make waves in the U.S. market. As part of German Accelerator’s U.S. Market Discovery AI program, founders pitch next-generation solutions built for lasting impact. Discover breakthrough and get a front-row seat to the future of AI.

https://luma.com/x44yh804

events.title: I Love Boosters
events.description: A crew of professional shoplifters take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven. It’s like community service.

events.title: Kiwi 101 at SXSW
events.description:
This informal, practical discussion is designed to share tips, tricks, and hard-won lessons on how to attend, survive, and flourish at one of the largest creative conferences in North America — without ending up in the wrong line, the wrong venue, or the wrong convo. Drinks and light bites will be served.

Please contact kimberly.marron@nzte.govt.nz for more information if you wish to attend.

events.title: Where Innovation Meets: A SXSW Reception
events.description: Reed Smith’s Global Emerging Technologies team invites you to an exclusive reception during SXSW 2026 – where founders, creators, dealmakers, and disruptors come together to spark new ideas and partnerships.Join us at Malverde, perched above Austin’s 2nd Street with stunning skyline views. Enjoy music from DJ Nixx and Mariachi Clasico and craft beverages and artisanal selections catered exclusively by acclaimed Mexican restaurant La Condesa while connecting with the boldest minds in tech, entertainment, and media.

events.title: Time and Water
events.description: Renowned Icelandic poet and author Andri Snær Magnason is chasing something elusive. As the glacial ice of his homeland melts, he constructs a cinematic time capsule to hold onto this moment and send it to the future, before everything he loves slips away. Using his own collected archives, his grandparents’ photographs, and films, as well as traditional songs and folktales, Andri interlaces his family’s story with that of the land around him. From Academy Award®-nominated director Sara Dosa, "Time and Water" is a universal reflection on the power of home and what it means to be alive amid profound epochal change.

events.title: First They Came for My College
events.description: On January 6, 2023, Republican Governor Ron DeSantis enacted a right-wing takeover of a public university called New College of Florida, targeting both its culture and unique academic program for an ultra-conservative makeover. Resistance is immediate, but the campus descends into chaos as powerful political actors make sweeping changes. Caught up in the mix are a group of intellectually curious young people from all sides of the political spectrum intent on completing their studies at New College, which has suddenly become ground zero in the culture wars.

events.title: Joybubbles
events.description: A boy discovers he can control the global telephone system by whistling a magic tone. Born blind and yearning for connection, his early obsession with the telephone sparks a subculture that shapes the future of hacking and technology.

events.title: The Truth and Tragedy of Moriah Wilson
events.description: An intimate, arresting portrait of cyclist Moriah Wilson—raised by a fierce, loving family—whose singular drive becomes her superpower, carrying her to athletic brilliance and, devastatingly, toward a life cut short by murder.
events.venue: Rollins Theatre at the Long Center

events.title: #Skyking
events.description: In exclusive interviews and air traffic control audio, #SKYKING tells the story of Horizon Air ground service agent Richard “Beebo” Russell, who clocked into work, stole a $33 million plane, and took off into the skies of the Pacific Northwest—embarking on a white-knuckle flight that came to embody the hopes, dreams, and despair of the American working class.

events.title: Erupcja
events.description: Set in Poland, Erupcja follows two women as they complicate their romantic lives. Nel lives in Warsaw where she works at a flower shop. When her childhood friend Bethany comes to visit with a new boyfriend, a volcano erupts.

events.title: Seekers of Infinite Love
events.description:
Kayla Bachman, an author who struggles with emotional connection, Zach Bachman, a lawyer who dreams of being a folk singer and Wes Bachman, a graphic novelist / gambling & pill addict, meet to discuss their younger sister Scarlett who joined a cult in Kentucky. 
Zach and his dysfunctional and absent parents have hired cult deprogrammer Rick Delacroix to help them rescue Scarlett. 
They embark on a roadtrip to save their sister, and bring their family together.

events.title: Sparks
events.description:
Cleo is new to Sparks, Nevada when she discovers a cigarette vending machine that inexplicably produces a book on Jean-Luc Godard. When she meets the Crop soon after, Cleo’s morphed into a cinephile, and when she learns of the Crop’s reservoir visits, she’s certain that she could time travel and meet Godard in 60s Paris.	

Crop leader Antoine is enamored with Cleo but rankled by her insinuations that Crop life is boring. When Cleo disappears at the reservoir, Antoine calls into question his own sense of purpose, before unexpected adventures materialize—a shootout, a dreamy gay barbecue—until Cleo returns to Sparks and the Crop must figure out where she’s been and if she’s lost her mind.

events.title: Susannah Joffe
events.venue: Austin City Limits Live at the Moody Theater

events.title: One Another
events.description: Sometimes it takes the end of something to know what is really at stake. Joe, Giorgia, and Lorri are all grappling with the possible end of an intimate friendship at vastly different stages of life: a cross-country move, a mental health crisis, and a shift into empty-nesting have forced them each to reevaluate the support they need from those closest to them. Chronicling three different friendships over the course of three years, "One Another" brings together verite with a wealth of personal archives to intertwine their journeys as they search for what it really means for us to care for each other. The result is a story of change, heartache, and connection in this ode to platonic love.

events.title: Ugly Cry
events.description: When Delaney's boyfriend leaves town to shoot a splashy zombie movie, she becomes obsessed with a character she’s auditioning for after she learns the producers think she has an "ugly cry." But when she tries to make her cry prettier, her performance suffers. Can she contort herself, and her face, to have the perfect cry? Her attempts to change herself cause Young Delaney to haunt her, catapulting present day Delaney deeper down the rabbit hole. She isolates herself and grows increasingly delusional, and interested in physical fixes to her acting problem. How can she make the world see her as she sees herself? How can she become and become and become? She will become famous. Or die trying.
