events.title: Baby/Girls
events.description: In post-Dobbs rural Arkansas, teen birth rates remain among the highest in the nation, shaped by generational patterns and limited access to sex education. For pregnant teenagers with limited family support, a Christian maternity home provides housing, prenatal care, and faith-based guidance. Filmed over two years with intimate verité access, Baby/Girls remains inside the house as three young women move through pregnancy, give birth, and step into motherhood. They come from families marked by poverty, addiction, and abuse; several are daughters of teen mothers themselves, continuing cycles that span generations. The film offers a powerful portrait of lives we often cannot see.

events.title: Drift
events.description: Isaac “Drift” Wright, a self-taught photographer and Army veteran haunted by trauma, finds healing through breathtaking, illegal climbs of the world’s tallest structures. But his pursuit of art sparks a high-stakes battle with law enforcement in this intimate portrait of risk, resilience, and freedom in modern America.

events.title: SXSW Community Service Awards Recognition: Vision Maker Media
events.description: The SXSW Community Service Awards celebrate leaders and non-profit organizations from Austin and around the world who work tirelessly to improve the standing of the specific groups and causes that they serve.Francene Blythe-Lewis currently serves as President and CEO of Vision Maker Media (VMM), the longest-running Native American media organization, and a cornerstone of Indigenous public broadcasting. As CEO, Blythe-Lewis is an established executive producer on award-winning documentaries and series, including Almost an Island, Searching for Sequoyah, IndigiGenius, Roots of Comedy with Jesus Trejo, Without Arrows, The Bears on Pine Ridge, and She Cried That Day. She emphasizes expanding the thematic range and contemporary visibility of Native stories in public media. Previously, Blythe-Lewis served as Director of Programs at the Native Arts and Cultures Foundation and as Director of National Geographic’s All Roads Film Project, where she redirected significant resources toward Indigenous filmmakers whereby cultivating long-term media careers for many that she supported worldwide. She has held visionary leadership roles at the Smithsonian Institution, and her professional impact is defined by building durable Indigenous media infrastructure—ensuring Native stories are created by Native people, supported by sustainable systems, and shared nationally with audiences and for posterity.

events.title: “It’s in Development” Creating Great TV for Global Platforms
events.description: From assessing pitches to staffing writers’ rooms to offering script notes and more, Universal Studio Group’s television executives dive-deep into their development processes and share what makes for a strong, mutually advantageous relationship between creators and a studio. Gain insights from the people behind recent & upcoming series, including The Five-Star Weekend, Ponies, We Were Liars, Cape Fear, Too Much, All Her Fault and many more.

events.title: Artist Demo Listening Session: Pop (Part 1)
events.description: Artist Demo Listening Sessions, Presented by Discovr Radio, at SXSW are an interactive format where attendees have the opportunity to play demos for music experts, sparking real-time feedback and meaningful industry connections. You must be present to have your music in the running to be heard! SXSW attendees not having demos played are encouraged to attend and listen in on the fun! Each session will be followed up a social hour. Physical submissions will not be accepted at the door. Demo’s will be played on a first-come, first-served basis and attendees must submit their demo’s prior to the day of the session  by 11:59pm.  Please carefully read and fill out the form below to officially submit your demo: https://airtable.com/appYFNh7bkKd8nmwh/pagfBEWaVPizme5jr/form

speakers.name: Sarah Nagourney
speakers.title: Platinum-Selling Songwriter/Producer and Host of She Creates Noise Podcast

events.title: Audible Dimensions: Expanding Story Through Spatial Audio
events.description:
As storytelling expands into extended reality media, such as immersive films, VR, MR, AI glasses and location-based installations, spatial audio is emerging as one of the key narrative forces. 

With today’s advanced head-mounted display technology, audiences expect not just 3D visuals but equally rich immersive sound that conveys presence, space and movement.

This panel explores the latest innovation in immersive sound technology and practical application from three different perspectives: software and hardware capabilities of hosting platforms, the spatial audio formats and content production workflows that bring these experiences to life.

speakers.name: Oliver Kadel
speakers.title: Senior Sound Technologist for Immersive Media

events.title: Beta Testing a City: Startups, Sidewalks & Robotics
events.description: What if a city could be beta tested like an app? In South Downtown Atlanta, tech entrepreneurs, investors, and community leaders are transforming 16 acres of historic real estate into a living lab for innovation, equity, and urban reinvention. This panel brings together the visionaries behind the movement to explore how startups, real estate, and even robot dogs are converging to reimagine what cities—and civic life—can look like in the 21st century.

speakers.name: Jay Bailey
speakers.title: President and CEO
speakers.company: H.J. Russell Innovation Center for Entrepreneurs

events.title: Building an Artist Identity & Sustainable Content Strategy
events.description: Every artist has a story, but not every artist knows how to tell it consistently. This session explores how musicians can define their brand identity and build a sustainable content strategy that supports long-term growth. We’ll break down practical methods for clarifying your creative voice, designing visual and emotional cohesion, and developing a posting rhythm that amplifies your music without burning you out. Perfect for emerging and mid-level artists looking to strengthen their connection with fans, media, and industry partners.

events.title: Come Play at Grief Camp: Healing with Story & Community
events.description: What if you could spend an hour at SXSW… at grief camp? A place where everyone’s been through something hard, and no one pretends they’re “fine.” Experience Camps is flipping the script on how we process grief through play, connection, and clinically informed practices. In this immersive workshop. clinically-trained counselors and facilitators will guide you through activities designed to explore the expression and processing of grief. It’s playful, messy, cathartic, and it’s for anyone ready to rethink grief and connection. Grievers and non-grievers are welcome!

events.title: The De-brief: Rethinking the Brand–Creator Relationship
events.description: This session explores the cultural phenomenon of “the debrief” in creator-brand collaboration. Industry experts in creator partnerships and branded content strategy will discuss how brands can rethink outdated briefing processes, focusing on building trust, embracing transparency, and creating content that fits naturally into creators' lives. Attendees will gain fresh insights on working with creators authentically, moving away from rigid briefs, and integrating brands seamlessly into their content.

speakers.name: Chloe Parsons
speakers.title: Director, Social Content and Engagement Strategy

events.title: Decoding Consciousness, Psychedelics, and the Mind
events.description: After a lifetime studying consciousness, famed neuroscientist Dr. Christof Koch had a profound, "no self, no memories, no time, no space, just terror and ecstasy" experience after deliberately taking a potent psychedelic. He argues, if we claim to be students of consciousness, we must explore its most dramatic manifestations.  This story launches into the most urgent questions of our time: What is consciousness, really? As AI rapidly advances and we grow complex "mini-brains" in labs, understanding what it means to "feel" or "be" is no longer just philosophy—it's critical for our future.

speakers.name: Christof Koch
speakers.title: Meritorious Investigator At The Allen Institute, Chief Scientist At The Tiny Blue Dot Foundation

events.title: DJ Jester the Filipino Fist
events.venue: Flatstock Stage @ Austin Marriott Downtown (Moontower Hall)

events.title: Documentary Short Program 2
events.description: Authentic storytelling that captivates, surprises, and excites.
events.venue: Rollins Theatre at the Long Center

events.title: Escaping Algorithmic Binds: Creators vs. Corporate Platforms
events.description: Creators and users are locked in digital “serfdom” by corporate social media’s algorithms and business models. Rabble, Bridget Todd, and Rudy Fraser will tackle how to break free from the feudal overlords of tech, and explain why Musk buying Twitter aided the move to decentralized apps. They’ll dig into new financial models, open protocols, and new community apps that empower creators and users without enriching platform owners. Learn how to create strategies that sustain social communities, and why open, user-first social apps are gaining in popularity with creators and audiences alike.

events.title: Featured Session: Jamie Lee Curtis. If Not Now, When, if Not Me, Who? Pivoting and Manifesting!
events.description: A conversation on how I am now a boss at 67!

events.title: Featured Session: Why Work Feels So Unfair and How Hard Conversations Help
events.description: Let's be honest: many managers would rather eat glass than tell you why you really didn't get the promotion, assignment, raise, or bonus. But their avoidance is creating a bigger problem - when leaders dodge difficult conversations, they create a vacuum where perceptions of unfairness flourish. Workplace expert Amy Gallo reveals how the inability (or unwillingness) to have hard conversations is eroding trust in organizations. You'll learn what transparency really looks like, how to demand the feedback you deserve, and why meritocracy is impossible without managers who can handle the heat.

events.title: The Future of Music is Participatory
events.description: The age of passive music consumption is ending. Today’s fans don’t just stream, they are stepping into the role of creator, collaborator, remixer. Driven by intuitive platforms, mobile-first production tools, and immersive technologies, the barriers to entry for music creation have never been lower. This panel explores how this shift is transforming the roles of artists, brands and platforms,from how songs are made to how artists connect with fans, and what tools and strategies are shaping this new creative era.

speakers.name: Jordy Freed
speakers.title: Senior Director, Deputy Head of Sony’s Personal Entertainment Business

events.title: GenMedia 101: Unlocking Creativity with AI & Google DeepMind
events.description: A hands-on session for artists, storytellers, and makers of all kinds. Build visuals, music, and media experiences - no code required. Every creative idea starts with a feeling: a scene in your mind, a sound in your head, or a story you keep coming back to. This workshop is for anyone who wants to bring those ideas to life, with a little help from generative AI. You’ll explore how tools like Veo (for video), Lyria (for music), and Nano Banana (for images) can help you shape what you imagine into something you can actually see, hear, and share. Laptop & headphones/earbuds recommended.

events.title: Global Connections Meet Up
events.description: In a time of global rupture, this SXSW Campfire brings founders, builders, and ecosystem leaders together to create new connections. Led by Brenda Balmares (Monterrey, Mexico) and Kevin Koym (Austin, Texas), the meetup centers on bridge-building, cross-border collaboration, and relationships that help navigate what comes next—and turn change into opportunity.

events.title: Going Off Script: Filmmaking Through an Indigenous Lens
events.description: Cherokee Film sits down with leading Native American directors and writers to discuss breaking into the industry, working in Hollywood, what's up next for independent film, and what they're binge watching right now.

events.title: How the Ocean Twilight Zone Regulates Our Climate
events.description: The mesopelagic zone, or Ocean Twilight Zone, where light begins to disappear, is home to creatures that are crucial to regulating our climate through the largest migration on the planet that locks away 2-6 gigatons of carbon every year. With improving technology and increasing demand for fish protein, industry is exploring ways to exploit these deep-sea animals for uses like fish oil and pet food. This session will showcase the amazing animals that live in the deep, their role in regulating our planet’s climate, and international efforts to keep this vital carbon pump functioning like it should.

events.title: I Bottled My Mother: The Mrs. Meyer's Story by Monica Nassif
events.description:
Monica Nassif didn’t just build a brand—she bottled a legacy. 
I Bottled My Mother is the gritty, hilarious, heartfelt origin story behind Mrs. Meyer’s Clean Day, the cult-favorite cleaning line inspired by Monica’s real-life mom, Thelma Meyer: a whip-smart, no-nonsense Midwesterner who raised nine children with little more than elbow grease, common sense, and a garden full of vegetables. Part startup manual, part memoir, this is the candid story of how one woman turned domestic skills into corporate strategy, and a small soap company into a household name.

events.title: Keep Calm & Flo On: Keeping an Enduring Icon Fresh & Funny
events.description:
How do you take a character from one TV spot to icon and keep her relevant, beloved & funny for 15+ years?
Join the creative team and the woman behind the white apron: Stephanie Courtney, AKA Flo. Alongside Progressive Insurance (brand), Arnold (agency) and Station (production) , she’ll help unpack how one ad grew into a universe of characters, comedic styles and unforgettable moments. From Flo’s personas, to red carpet parodies and blockbuster genre spoofs, this campaign has done it all. Expect BTS stories, comedic insights and lessons on longevity in an industry that often chases the new.

events.title: The Knowledge Paradox: When Does Sharing Become Theft?
events.description: For decades, the open movement championed sharing as the path to knowledge equity—billions of works freely accessible and reusable across research, education, and culture. But AI weaponizes that openness: what was built to democratize knowledge now trains models that concentrate power and profit. Open data scraping. Closed model development. Free content fueling extraction. As we mark Creative Commons' 25th anniversary, we confront an impossible question: how do we keep knowledge open without enabling its exploitation?

speakers.name: Lawrence Lessig
speakers.title: Roy L. Furman Professor of Law and Leadership

events.title: Look What You Made Me Do: Revenge as Creative Catalyst
events.description: Beyoncé did it. Kendrick did it. Taylor did it. Now it’s your turn. This immersive workshop (with a killer soundtrack) turns rejection, rivalry, and resentment into creative fire. From The Count of Monte Cristo to Kill Bill, we’ll channel iconic revenge arcs, neuroscience insights, and pop power plays. In doing so, we'll reframe past slights as story fuel, sharpen your personal or professional brand, and turn petty into power moves. Part life strategy, part anti-hero training camp, this is your chance to alchemize grudge into growth. Who said motivation had to be pure?

events.title: The Masters: A Digital Experience Unlike Any Other
events.description:
Long recognized for its rich heritage and time-honored traditions, the Masters Tournament has been home to some of golf’s greatest moments. But few know that behind the blooming azaleas and towering pines is a cutting-edge technology and data operation bringing the storied greens of Augusta National Golf Club to life for millions of fans worldwide.

In this session, IBM pulls back the curtain on its 35-year partnership with ANGC. From launching Masters.com in 1996, to building “the best app in sports,” to pioneering the use of genAI for player projections, real-time shot tracking, analysis and more — all designed to enhance the fan experience without compromising the tournament’s timeless character.

events.description: Learn how big corporations are betting on millennial CEOs to reinvigorate legacy brands and drive new growth. Meet three young CEOs - all from underrepresented backgrounds - who have each taken different paths to the C-Suite in industries ranging from fitness to tech. A candid, high-energy conversation for aspiring future leaders.

events.title: Modern Makers Meet Up
events.description: Making is evolving from traditional craft to digital storytelling. In the era of social media, we’re finding more creators showcase their physical talents online. This Meet Up brings together modern makers working with diverse materials, platforms, and disciplines who are redefining what it means to create today. Whether you’re building by hand, sharing your process online, or blending the physical and digital, this is a space to connect, exchange ideas, and find others shaping the future of making.

events.title: A New Era of Brand-Creator Partnerships
events.description: Successful brand–creator relationships have moved beyond one-off sponsored posts. Now, brands are building long-term collaborations grounded in authenticity — not just treating creators like media buys. Join Lia Haberman as she discusses the future of this evolving landscape with brand leaders Carly Gomez, Josh Line and John Sullivan. They’ll discuss current trends like co-creation and employee brand ambassador programs as well as the future of where they think these relationships are heading.

speakers.name: Lia Haberman
speakers.title: Creator Economy And Influencer Marketing Expert And Author Of The Icymi Newsletter

events.title: The New Era of Women in Music
events.description: From the pay gap and barriers to safer spaces and breakthrough wins — women and gender-expansive voices in music are demanding more than representation. They’re building a new industry. This session brings artists, execs, and advocates together to explore where we are, what’s still in the way, and how we move forward. Expect bold ideas, real talk, and actionable steps to drive change and empower the next generation.

speakers.name: Janishia Jones
speakers.title: Founder / Researcher
speakers.company: A Seat at the Table Market Research Agency

events.title: The Next Five Years of Private Markets: What Founders Can’t Afford to Miss
events.description: In today’s market, the challenge isn’t finding opportunities, it’s finding signal in the noise. Join Nizar Tarhuni, EVP of Research & Market Intelligence at PitchBook, and a leading investor for a data-driven conversation on where capital is flowing in 2026, the signals investors care about most, how AI is reshaping sourcing and diligence, and what current dynamics mean for fundraising and valuation strategy. Founders will gain a clear view into how investors are making decisions—and how to position their companies to stand out and get funded.

speakers.name: Nizar Tarhuni
speakers.title: Executive Vice President, Research & Market Intelligence

events.title: Own Your Sh*t (and Your IP): The Creator CEO Playbook
events.description: Most creators don’t get screwed in dramatic blowups. They sign their rights away quietly in contracts that look “standard.” In fact, 6 out of 10 creators don’t realize they’ve given up ownership until it’s already gone. This isn’t a legal lecture. It’s a hard reset on how creators should think about IP, licensing, and leverage before agreeing to the deal. The Creator CEO Playbook shows how to spot ownership traps early and stop trading long-term assets for one-time checks.

speakers.name: Kristina Liburd
speakers.title: Creator Ownership Strategist Founder, Creator Law School

events.title: The Playbook: Viral Hits to Loyal Fandoms
events.description: It’s never been easier to get 10 million views—and never harder to turn that into a fan who buys a ticket. This advanced session breaks down how top artist teams use fan signals from short-form content to build brands that outlast trends. Hear real stories of how UGC patterns, platform data, and community insights drive visuals, merch, partnerships, and tours—turning virality into real demand. Expect honest lessons on what flops, what scales, and why every viral moment needs a long-term loyalty plan.

events.title: Protecting Visual Storytelling: Tools for Radical Transparency in a Post-Truth Era
events.description: Synthetic media (AI-generated photo and video) increasingly undermines public trust in news imagery at a time when democratic resilience depends on accurate, verifiable information. This panel unpacks the adaptation of “radical” transparency as a tool for re-establishing public trust and cultivating audience literacy in the face of AI’s growing influence. Visual journalists and strategists will tackle how to establish image integrity in an AI-saturated world; why robust attribution and transparency is a key path forward in rebuilding public trust and is a news sustainability practice.

speakers.name: Marie De Jesús
speakers.title: Director, Pictures Of The Year International
speakers.company: Reynolds Journalism Institute, University of Missouri School of Journalism

speakers.name: Coleen Jose
speakers.title: Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Content Authenticity

events.title: The Rising Power of the Female Homebuyer
events.description: Homeownership remains one of the most powerful drivers of generational wealth, shaping financial security, stability, and long-term opportunity. This panel will unpack the cost of waiting to buy a home, the rising influence of intergenerational transfers, and the different forms of wealth a home creates. Together, we’ll explore what it will take to preserve homeownership as a pathway to prosperity for future generations.

events.title: Round Table: Acting: Alexandra Barreto, Alyssa Rodriguez, and Rider Strong
events.description: An extension of our popular Mentor Sessions, our Round Table Sessions not only allow attendees to learn from the industry experts that sit at each of the three tables in this session but they also allow attendees to learn from the questions and experiences of their peers as well. This Round Table Session will bring together industry experts and SXSW attendees for an enlightening discussion on Acting.

events.title: Securing Agency: Ownership in the Era of AI
events.description: As AI agents begin to act on our behalf—signing contracts, moving value, and managing data—we face a new crisis of authority: How does an autonomous system prove it truly represents you? Ian Rogers, Ledger CXO, explores the evolution of ownership and control in an AI-native world. This session moves beyond protecting assets to securing human intent. Discover why cryptographic signing and hardware-backed control are the essential layers for a responsible agent economy. Learn how to embrace the massive potential of AI without sacrificing autonomy or the human root of trust.

events.title: Space Technology and Innovation Conversation
events.description: Have an idea that could launch the space industry into its next era? Join a vibrant gathering of space tech pioneers, passionate enthusiasts, and established space professionals. This is your platform to pitch innovative concepts, receive feedback on new and expanding ideas, and forge powerful connections. Come to share, learn, and collaborate with the brightest minds charting the future of space.

events.title: Superconnector Meet Up
events.description: Superconnectors' - those who seem hyper-connected to large networks of people - are naturally drawn to SXSW. They thrive in a creative and innovative environment like SXSW which affords countless opportunities to meet interesting people. In its third year at SXSW, the Superconnectors Meet Up is intentionally designed to give business development professionals a place to network with other business leaders.

events.title: SXSW Pitch-Enterprise and Future of Work
events.description:
The SXSW Pitch provides a platform for early-stage technology startups to present their groundbreaking products and services to a panel of distinguished industry experts, influential media professionals, and leading venture capitalists and angel investors.

On Saturday, March 14, five innovative companies will take the stage in Salon FGH at the JW Marriott, showcasing their ideas, innovations, and entrepreneurial vision before a live audience and judging panel. Come be inspired by the next generation of tech innovators shaping the future.

Enterprise and Future of WorkTechnologies and platforms that empower organizations to operate more efficiently, securely, and intelligently in an increasingly connected world—while reimagining how, where, and why work gets done. This category includes Enterprise SaaS solutions that drive scalable business operations across departments including sales and Human Resources. It also covers Vertical SaaS tailored to the specialized needs of a variety of industries. Startups in this space leverage AI/ML for Enterprise to power decision support systems, workflow automation, predictive analytics, and intelligent process augmentation. Additional focus areas include project management, human capital systems, APIs, knowledge management, cloud computing, MLOps, and AI-driven customer service—tools that collectively shape the future of work, business intelligence, and enterprise growth at scale. These innovations often focus on simplifying processes through innovative workflows and intelligent design, enabling more efficient and personalized user experiences across enterprise functions. Solutions may also incorporate personalization across enterprise functions, as well as platforms that support both businesses and individuals in navigating modern productivity demands.

Winner of the Enterprise and Future of Work Technologies will be announced at the Award Ceremony, Saturday, March 14th at 6:30pm.

events.title: User Centric Design & Funding of Accessible Tech
events.description: This panel will focus on user centered design (UCD) as the crux of successful product development - with inclusion at the core. Founders with disabilities will discuss their experiences developing technology and services - focusing on how they undertook UCD, identified testers in their communities, and ultimately - funded those initiatives and brought them to market.

events.title: Where Should We Begin? Live with Esther Perel
events.description: Join iconic psychotherapist Esther Perel for a special live-taping of her acclaimed podcast, Where Should We Begin?, where she speaks with real people in search of insight baring the raw, intimate, and profound details of their stories.

events.title: Why You're Culturally Irrelevant (...And How to Change That)
events.description: Data is essential—but it can also be a hiding place. When we over-rely on dashboards, chase the same trends as competitors, and optimize for algorithms, we play it safe, yet lose relevance. There's a better approach for cultural resonance: stop chasing culture and begin shaping it. Through frameworks, case studies, how-to's and data, we'll explore how organizations can move beyond reactionary trend hijacking, and instead author preferred futures alongside communities. The most culturally resonant brands aren't chasing, they're making. What future will you build?

events.title: Women in Film & Televison Austin Hosts Connect & Collaborate
events.description: Women in Film & Television Austin hosts Connect & Collaborate, a meet-and-greet meant to be a fun pause in the day where creatives come together. It’s about conversation and community.

speakers.name: Erica Deiparine-Sugars
speakers.title: Advisory Board Member
speakers.company: Women in Film and Television Austin

events.title: The World’s Game, Our Stage: FOX Previews FIFA World Cup 2026
events.description: This summer, the world’s greatest sporting event FIFA WORLD CUP returns to the U.S. for the first time in three decades. But this isn’t just any event, FIFA WORLD CUP 2026 promises to deliver a cultural moment that defines a generation. FOX Sports broadcasters and U.S. Soccer legends Alexi Lalas, Stu Holden and Carli Lloyd talk with acclaimed host and reporter Jenny Taft, reflecting on the evolution of the beautiful game in America and preview what’s in store for millions of viewers when FOX presents the biggest World Cup ever.

events.title: Your First 90 Days as a Creator from Experts at Meta, YouTube & Snapchat
events.description: In this rare cross platform conversation, moderated by acclaimed creator strategist Antonia Alakija, creator partnerships leaders from Meta, YouTube & Snapchat come together to break down what creators should focus on in their first 90 days of taking content seriously. We’ll explore how fast growing creators structure early momentum, the common pitfalls that derail progress & strategies for building an audience with intention. From platform-specific insights to proven growth frameworks, this session offers an honest tactical roadmap for turning creative potential into a lasting personal brand.

events.title: Money Mark
events.description: Legendary composer, inventor, and the unofficial “Fourth Beastie Boy,” Money Mark has been rewriting the sonic playbook since ’75. With a career spanning Billboard #1s and collaborations with icons like David Byrne, Jack White, Miley Cyrus, and Beck, he is the ultimate musical pivot point. Part virtuoso, part mad scientist, Mark currently spends his time inventing new instruments and using unconventional experiments to find the sounds of tomorrow.
events.venue: Flatstock Stage @ Austin Marriott Downtown (Moontower Hall)

events.title: The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist
events.description: A father-to-be tries to figure out what is happening with the AI insanity, exploring the existential dangers and stunning promise of this technology that humanity has created.

events.title: Chili Finger
events.description: When Jessica Lipki discovers a severed human finger in her bowl of chili, she recognizes an opportunity to seize control of her stagnating life. Jess blackmails the regionally-beloved fast-food chain for $100,000 in return that she and her blissfully ignorant husband, Ron, keep quiet about the incident. Unbeknownst to Jess, her stunt has caught the attention of "the" Blake Junior, the plutocratic founder behind the "Blake Junior’s" food empire. He recruits his ex-marine buddy, Dave, to investigate Jess and discover the truth behind the chili finger...

events.title: Manhood
events.description: "Manhood" follows Dallas entrepreneur Bill Moore as he attempts to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox. Along the way, an OnlyFans star and a father of five put their bodies—and their insecurities—on the line. Blending dark humor with unexpected empathy, "Manhood" examines shame, addiction, and the fragile myths of American masculinity. From Executive Producers World of Wonder ("RuPaul’s Drag Race"), Sheila Nevins ("Real Sex"), Penny Lane ("Hail Satan"), Producer Kerry Mack ("Proof of Concept"), and Director Daniel Lombroso ("White Noise").

events.title: Independent TV Pilot Program
events.description: Discover new pilots from indie talent.

events.title: Innovation Clubhouse Rooftop Happy Hour with SXSW London
events.description:
Sorry Austin, but there’s nowhere quite like London.

While other countries separate industries by city, we chuck everyone together — government, world‑class universities, finance, tech, music, fashion and art.

To celebrate this convergence, we’re hosting a happy hour at the Innovation Clubhouse, and we’d love you to join us for some drinks.

Connect with attendees, get inspired, and hear why SXSW London is the place to Shape The Future, 1–6 June 2026.

events.title: The Man with the Big Hat
events.description:
An unsung pioneer of 1970s Texas Progressive Country, Steven Fromholz had a knack for snatching defeat from the jaws of victory. Revered by legends like Willie Nelson, Lyle Lovett & John Denver, he remained commercially unknown. He sought redemption on the Rio Grande as a river guide until a debilitating stroke erased his musical memory, stripping Fromholz of his artistic identity.
This intimate and impressionistic portrayal, bolstered by newly discovered archives as well as never-before-heard recordings, unveils the evolution of Fromholz, and reshapes the notion of success and artistic fortitude.

events.title: The Sophs
events.description: The Sophs is a multi-genre six-piece hailing from Los Angeles, California, who’s confessional lyrics and nostalgic instrumentation make a statement regardless of whether they intend to or not
events.venue: Radio Day Stage @ Downright Austin Backyard

events.title: Thanks for Nothing
events.description: Katharina, Ricky, Malou, and Victoria live in a self-made anarchist group home - no parents, no school, no rules. Under the loose watch of social worker Ballack, things are going pretty well. But Katharina doesn’t want to live past 18, and her birthday is two weeks away. Her friends scramble to hide her suicide attempts, afraid the truth will destroy the only “home” they’ve ever had. In this darkly comedic tale of rebellion, abandonment, and surviving the absurd, "Thanks For Nothing" is the kids' collective FU to the adults who’ve abandoned or failed them.

events.title: Ugly Cry
events.description: When Delaney's boyfriend leaves town to shoot a splashy zombie movie, she becomes obsessed with a character she’s auditioning for after she learns the producers think she has an "ugly cry." But when she tries to make her cry prettier, her performance suffers. Can she contort herself, and her face, to have the perfect cry? Her attempts to change herself cause Young Delaney to haunt her, catapulting present day Delaney deeper down the rabbit hole. She isolates herself and grows increasingly delusional, and interested in physical fixes to her acting problem. How can she make the world see her as she sees herself? How can she become and become and become? She will become famous. Or die trying.

events.title: Brian
events.description: It sucks to be Brian. He’s smart, funny, and capable, but his mental health issues make it hard for anyone to see it - especially when compared to his effortlessly cool older brother. At school, Brian harbors an unrequited crush on Brooke: she’s smart, kind, pretty… and very much his teacher. A disastrous drama club audition leads to yet another one of Brian’s trademark public meltdowns. Thus begins Brian’s search for his new “thing”. On paper he’s chosen the worst possible fit: running for class president. With help from his therapist and the new kid, Justin, Brian launches his high-stakes campaign and sparks a messy, exquisitely awkward journey toward self-acceptance.

events.title: The Next Creative Frontier: Emerging Technology in Service of Storytelling
events.description:
Join Walt Disney Studios CTO Eddie Drake and StudioLAB VP Sonia Doshi for a fireside conversation on how emerging technologies are shaping the next era of storytelling. Moderated by Accenture, StudioLAB’s innovation partner, the discussion will explore how new tools can meaningfully empower creatives, expand storytelling formats, and deepen audience connection at a pivotal moment for the industry, while preserving creative excellence as the ultimate differentiator.
Speakers:
Sonia Doshi, VP Strategic Operations, Design & Production, Disney Eddie Drake, CTO Disney Studios Mary Hamilton, Innovation R&D Director, Accenture Jimmy Priestas, CMT AI and Data Lead, Americas, Accenture

events.title: Stages
events.description: It's make or break time for Ben Garza as he embarks on his solo first tour after the collapse of his band. By his side are Rita, his former tour manager stepping away from her stable life to help him, and Parker, a remaining bandmate who joins Ben as a utility player. However, Rita also secures Jessie Ramos as the opening act, a rising star whose sudden surge in popularity will completely destabilize Ben. Throughout this musical odyssey, Ben will face characters on the road who challenge his ideas of success, relevance, and purpose. Some encounters offer hope; others deepen his doubt. By the tour’s end, Ben must decide whether to keep chasing the life he once had—or chart a new path forward.

events.title: Annual Legal Update for Indie Film and TV
events.description:
Chris Perez and his partners Michael Donaldson and Dale Nelson will be back for another lively
(and surprisingly entertaining) update on the many legal developments affecting the indie film
community.

The distribution landscape has once again changed since last we were together at SXSW.  While the number of buyers for independent films seems to have contracted, numbers show that the theatrical business is alive and well, and films are still getting financed and produced. The Trump administration has cut funding for public television, affecting the documentary film market. New distribution models have sprung up, and self-distribution is once again a popular route.

Since last year, several legal issues have come to the fore. The topic that continues to take
shape from a legal standpoint is AI. What do you need to be concerned about as a user of
GenAI content? As a creator, should you be concerned about use of your works to train LLMs?
We will explore the ever-evolving legal landscape when it comes to AI.

Fair use continues to be a useful tool for both documentary and scripted filmmakers, so we’ll
cover the latest fair use cases affecting filmmakers.

Films based on or inspired by a true story continue to not only be popular among viewers but
have also led to a number of important lawsuits.

Bring all your burning questions, because these three leaders in the indie industry tend to stay
on to help you learn more about anything you need to know.

events.title: Artificial Imagination and The Fiction After Cinema
events.description: This conference examines how AI, beyond cost reduction and visual effects, inaugurates a post-photographic rupture. Cinema's factuality—rooted in photographic capture of what was—confronts AI's counterfactuality: statistical generation of what could be, freed from indexical constraints. After metabolizing cinematic language, AI opens unprecedented fictional territories: evolving generative narratives, multiversal storytelling, dissolution of boundaries between creation and reception. We explore these new fictions that transcend filming constraints and classical narration, revealing how counterfactual generation catalyzes an anthropological mutation of our fictional regimes, and a means of resistance to the dissolution of common truth.

events.title: The Burnout Economy: Leading in an Age of Exhaustion
events.description: Exhaustion is no longer just a personal issue—it’s now an economic concern. Leaders across industries are burning out, leading to short-term thinking and diminished organizational resilience. Dr Daniel Motta will draw on research in economics, organizational behavior, and leadership to show how exhausted executives impact everything from market performance to employee engagement and introduces new frameworks for fostering sustainable leadership that safeguards both people and performance.

events.title: Creativity, Commerce & Chaos: Tech & Indie Filmmaking
events.description: As AI transforms how we create and consume media, quiet revolutions are happening behind the scenes: creators, producers, agents, and technologists are building the infrastructure to track, protect, and monetize creativity across its entire lifecycle. This panel brings together a first-time filmmaker, a veteran distributor, a top agent, and an AI platform CEO to explore how attribution, metadata, royalty tracking, and ethical packaging are becoming essential to creative business.

events.title: The Death of Passive Entertainment–A Future for Participants
events.description: Pop culture isn't just consumed—it's lived. A song or movie will spark IRL activity like themed workouts, sold-out dining experiences or fan meetups (e.g. Love Island events +4,950% in the past year). This shift from passive watching to active gathering reshapes culture and moves people–physically. Fandoms are inspiring creator-led experiences, turning local spaces into cultural venues overnight. In this panel Julia Hartz (Eventbrite), Dani Calogera (What/If), Kate Wolff (Lupine Creative) & David Salazar (Fast Company) explore how pop culture becomes a springboard for real connection.

events.title: Exotic Thinking: Outsmarting AI with Human Creativity
events.description: In the foresight world, staying brilliant in the Age of the Algorithm demands more than just tech fluency—it requires radical creativity. In this book reading, technofuturist Sarah DaVanzo and AI pioneer Miro Dimitrov explore how we can outthink AI using paradox, taboo, and cognitive disobedience. Drawing from Sarah’s forthcoming book Exotic Thinking, the session offers a provocative path to rewiring human ingenuity in a future shaped by machines.

events.title: Experiential Marketing Meet Up
events.description: Join fellow creatives, artists, producers, and brand and agency leaders for an engaging meetup centred on experiential marketing and immersive experiences. Whether you're here to exchange ideas, find collaborators, or get inspired, this event is designed to spark meaningful connections. A fun, participant-led icebreaker will help kickstart the conversation.

events.title: Exploring New Dimensions of IRL Entertainment
events.description: We’re in an age of experiences. More than ever, the proliferation of virtual connection has driven a hunger for IRL experiences that blend physical and digital to create “wow” moments and lasting memories. In this session, Bonnie Rosen, GM of the Disney Accelerator, will speak with the founders of Liminal Space and Haddy about how holographic displays and custom AI-powered 3D printing techniques can transform any space to create immersive moments, and how quickly these materials can be reconfigured, reused, and reimagined again and again for new audiences.

events.title: Featured Session: A Conversation with Garry Tan
events.description: Hear from the President & CEO of Y Combinator. In addition to his Featured Session, Garry Tan will co-emcee the SXSW Pitch 2026 Award Ceremony.

events.title: Featured Session: How Crypto is Building New Capital Markets for Everyone, not just Wall Street
events.description: For years, crypto was criticized as a solution searching for a problem. The on-chain creator economy failed to gain momentum, and the concept of ownership reflected less on community governance and more on self-custody. But something shifted. As crypto activity became increasingly financialized, the infrastructure built to support it quietly unlocked something bigger—new pathways for creators and everyday users to participate in capital markets once reserved for institutions. Join Pedro Miranda, Head of Consumer at the Solana Foundation, and Rodolfo Gonzalez from Foundation Capital as we examine what's changed in the on-chain economy and explore the emerging consumer crypto landscape that's democratizing access to financial opportunity.

events.title: Featured Session: The Mythical Model: Next Gen Creator-Brand Partnerships
events.description: Digital ad spend will hit $600 billion this year, with brands expected to shift more budget to creators. But how can creators themselves tap this massive opportunity? Rhett & Link, legendary creators and hosts of Good Mythical Morning, will discuss their innovative brand partnership model — built on 360 campaigns, programmatic ads, sponsorships, direct integrations, and the latest brand matching technology — and how other creators can unlock new revenue opportunities to create lasting careers.

events.title: Future of Loyalty: Gen Z and Gen Alpha will shape a new era
events.description: Born in the age of the internet and now Generative AI, Gen Z and Gen Alpha are the most digitally savvy segments we’ve ever seen. But they also have differing expectations for authenticity, connection, and IRL experiences. How well brands meet their unique needs could make or break their ability to foster long-term loyalty. Marketing executives will discuss the nuances, as well as the tactics already in place to reach Gen Z and prepare for Gen Alpha. Both generations continue to raise the bar, and the pressure is on brands to deliver IRL connections now and in the years to come.

events.title: Housing: The Key to the American Dream
events.description: Homeownership remains one of the most powerful drivers of generational wealth, shaping financial security, stability, and long-term opportunity. This panel will unpack the cost of waiting to buy a home, the rising influence of intergenerational transfers, and the different forms of wealth a home creates. Together, we’ll explore what it will take to preserve homeownership as a pathway to prosperity for future generations.

events.title: An Influential Conversation with Jordan "The Stallion"
events.description: Join us for an engaging fireside chat featuring Influential Chief Communications Officer, Chris Detert, in conversation with one of today’s most recognizable digital personalities, Jordan “The Stallion” Howlett. Known for his infectious energy, unfiltered honesty, and viral storytelling across platforms like TikTok, Jordan has become a leading voice in the creator economy. From his signature food reviews to his candid takes on everyday life, he’s built a devoted community by staying true to himself—while navigating the business of brand deals, audience engagement, and online growth.

events.title: Is Reinforcement Learning the Real Future of AI?
events.description: While AGI, generative AI, and humanoid robots dominate the spotlight, reinforcement learning (RL) is quietly powering the next chapter of AI. Unlike other methods, RL enables systems to learn by doing – adapting through trial and error in dynamic environments. In this session, one of the world’s leading RL minds will explore why this approach is essential for building truly autonomous, intelligent systems, and how today’s breakthroughs are laying the groundwork for the next wave of transformative AI.

speakers.name: Peter Stone

events.title: It’s Not Too Late: Art and Technology Can Unf*ck the Future
events.description: An honest, wide-angle conversation about technology, art, and possibility at a moment defined by polarization, climate disruption, and media fatigue. Neither a defense nor a rejection of technology, this panel explores what emerging and immersive media enable when paired with human agency, creativity, and care. Panelists grapple with real harm and real possibility, discussing how storytelling can connect us rather than divide us and help move beyond doom-and-gloom toward inspiration, imagination, and collective repair.

events.title: Keeping It Real: AI, Human Data, and the Future of Brand Connections
events.description:
Brands are racing to adopt efficient, prompt-driven systems. But as we continue building a world optimized for machines, how do brands stay meaningful to people?

Join Chris Manzini, Head of Global Communications for PepsiCo and Billy Jones, CMO of Hootsuite powered by TalkwalkerAI, as they share their thoughts on  navigating artificial intelligence in a human world.

This isn’t just another debate about AI hype. It will be a real conversation about where AI helps brands understand people better—and where it quietly creates trust, culture, or reputation risks in ways leaders can’t ignore.

events.title: Melanie Dyer
events.description:
Growing up on her family's farm in Mount Russell, regional Australia, Melanie Dyer started crafting her stories into songs at the age of twelve. With an authentic blend of her down-to-earth farm girl roots, dynamic stage presence and catchy contemporary songwriting chops, Melanie has performed at some of the world's biggest country festivals, including CMA Fest in Nashville, CMC Rocks, and the Big Red Bash in Australia. As a talented artist and songwriter, Melanie has racked up multiple #1 country radio hits and earned three nominations for Most Performed Country Work at the APRA Awards. 
With over 12.5 million streams, her chart-topping albums Fresh and Between You and Me have garnered her prestigious Golden Guitar nominations and the coveted APRA Professional Development Award. Her breakout hit Memphis T-Shirt catapulted her into the mainstream spotlight on commercial radio networks and a remarkable six-week stint at number one on the Australian Country Hot 50 Chart. In 2025 Melanie relocated to Nashville, Tennessee to chase her dreams of building a global audience and sharing her music across the USA.

events.title: Music Marketing: How to Stretch Releases for Years
events.description: You’ve dropped the track and pushed the promo. Now what? In a world where music moves fast, long-term visibility can still be more powerful than launch-week hype. In this panel, we’ll cover how artists and their teams extend the life of a release well beyond its debut. We’ll dig into smart reusable content, creative repackaging, how to keep songs fresh for fans, and how to turn "catalog" tracks into new campaign strategies. Expect practical strategies that keep fans engaged, music marketing momentum moving, and allow artists to stay in the spotlight for longer. With the right game plan, one release can sustain impact for years.

events.title: The New Cool: Choosing Moderation in a World of Excess
events.description: New generations are redefining consumption, choosing balance, moderation, meaning, and authenticity over excess. Using Georgetown University’s case study of AB InBev’s Global Smart Drinking Goals, this session explores how brands can leverage marketing expertise and innovations that meet consumers’ desire for more balanced choices, such as lower and no-alcohol beer, and influence to shape social norms and create shared value. The discussion highlights how purpose-driven strategies can drive behavior change, reinforce positive behaviors, promote moderation, and deliver sustainable growth.

events.title: OpenAI & Spurs: Building Human-Centered AI for Fans, Partners, and Communities
events.description: How do you scale AI without losing the human touch? In this session, leaders from the San Antonio Spurs and OpenAI share how they’re using AI to create more meaningful experiences for fans, partners, and communities. From personalized fan engagement and family-focused experiences to internal productivity and decision-making, the Spurs offer a real-world look at how purpose-built AI tools are being used on and off the court. Attendees will walk away with practical lessons on responsible AI adoption, concrete use cases from a global sports franchise, and a blueprint for putting people first while bringing cutting-edge technology to the courtside.

events.title: Our Lying Eyes: Climate Storytelling in a World of Misinformation
events.description: When we can't open our phones without being bombarded with deep fakes and half-truths, when we are told not to believe what we see with our own two eyes—it's hard not to feel destabilized Centered on the upcoming film The Weatherman, this panel explores how extreme weather survivor stories create the shared understanding that drives powerful social movements and policy change. Join filmmakers, local survivors, and policymakers to discover how real stories about the personal and economic impacts of extreme weather—told through the lens of film—can lead to real change.

events.title: The Patient Frame: Cinematic Creators in a Clickbait World
events.description: In a world of endless scrolling, a new wave of YouTube creators is choosing depth over speed. Led by Kariza Santos—known for her poetic voice and cinematic eye—this panel explores how treating uploads like short films, not content drops, is reshaping audience expectations and production norms. Together, we’ll examine why a slower, more intentional approach isn’t just possible in today’s fast-paced landscape—it’s essential to the future of digital storytelling.

events.title: Reinvention Not Repetition: Shifting the Innovation Mindset
events.description: In a disruptive era, innovation needs to be agile, inclusive, and driven by purpose. It’s essential to move quickly and address issues by transitioning from endless MVP cycles to iterative approaches that integrate technology with human-centered design, ethics, and resilience. This panel discusses how founders, creators, and corporate innovators can leverage AI, automation, and digital collaboration to balance profit with purpose, support internal disruptors, and foster cultures where innovation delivers genuine value.

events.title: Round Table: Development: Carolina Tamez and Henry Kittredge
events.description: An extension of our popular Mentor Sessions, our Round Table Sessions not only allow attendees to learn from the industry experts that sit at each of the three tables in this session but they also allow attendees to learn from the questions and experiences of their peers as well. This Round Table Session will bring together industry experts and SXSW attendees for an enlightening discussion on Development.

events.title: Sober Space Meet Up - 3/14
events.description: Sober Space is a welcoming gathering place for people in all forms of recovery during SXSW 2026. This space hosts all-format recovery meetings for Friends of Bill and all SXSW attendees who are seeking a supportive meeting environment during the festival. Participants are invited to sit together and share experience, strength, and hope in a confidential, judgment-free setting. Meetings are facilitated by The SIMS Foundation alongside trusted leaders from the recovery community.

events.title: State of the DIY Artist
events.description: Abe Batshon (BeatStars) and Curtiss King map how creators are building careers on their own terms — from publishing and direct monetization to growing audiences and protecting IP. Expect actionable tactics, honest tradeoffs, and a live Q&A that gives producers and indie artists the step-by-step playbook to level up.

events.title: Streaming, Shorts & AI: Where Are Your Royalties Going?
events.description: The royalty landscape has never been more fragmented — or more ripe for missed income. As short-form video, UGC remixes, micro-sync, and AI-generated content explode, artists and rights holders are fighting to keep payments transparent and fair. This session brings together leaders to unpack where the biggest royalty “black holes” are hiding now, why legacy collection models can’t keep up, and how direct licensing, better data, and new tech are helping close the gap. Expect real-world examples of found money and clear steps artists can take to plug revenue leaks before they happen.

events.title: Swiftie Meet Up
events.description: Whether you’ve been a fan since “Beautiful Eyes,” or you just discovered her when you were dragged to see “The Eras Tour” in theaters by a fanatical friend, you’re welcome at this Meet Up for Swifties at SXSW. Friendship bracelet trading encouraged but not required.

events.title: SXSW Pitch-Innovative World Tech
events.description:
The SXSW Pitch provides a platform for early-stage technology startups to present their groundbreaking products and services to a panel of distinguished industry experts, influential media professionals, and leading venture capitalists and angel investors.

On Saturday, March 14, five innovative companies will take the stage in Salon FGH at the JW Marriott, showcasing their ideas, innovations, and entrepreneurial vision before a live audience and judging panel. Come be inspired by the next generation of tech innovators shaping the future.

This category is for any creative and innovative application, product, or service that does not fit in another SXSW Pitch category, as well as technologies that act as the infrastructure that new technologies are built on. Examples that might fit into this category include (but are not limited to) societal good, biodegradable materials, decentralized energy grids, neuromorphic computing, social media platforms, aerospace, nanotechnology, pet tech, quantum computing and computer chip technology, and others.

Winner of the Innovative World Technologies will be announced at the Award Ceremony, Saturday, March 14th at 6:30pm.

events.title: Tefi Talks Live
events.description: Tefi is your favorite work bestie who’s always ready to yap about celebrities, read their star charts, give romantic advice, and be your best excuse to avoid the actual work. In this special live episode of her podcast Tefi Talks, you can expect sharp reflections on celebrity, astrology, and modern life featuring a special guest.

events.title: Virtual (un)Reality – From Music to Immersive Storytelling
events.description: Can a song become a world? This panel explores how composer Philippe Cohen Solal transformed a music album into an expanded transmedia narrative. We’ll dive into the creation process to adapt music compositions to new forms of immersive interaction that led to the creation of the VR musical experience INSIDER-OUTSIDER. From DJ culture to tango revival, outsider art and virtual reality, we’ll discuss how culture remix and hybrid musical formats fuel new creative languages and audience engagement across physical and virtual spaces.

events.title: What else...what else…with Michael Cruz Kayne
events.description: Get ready for a unique blend of hilarity and introspection as Audible presents a live episode featuring the talented comedian Michael Cruz Kayne and special guest comedian, Chloe Radcliffe. Kayne, known for his sharp wit and poignant observations, brings his distinctive brand of humor to the SXSW stage with an engaging 40-minute session offering an intimate look into the world of stand-up comedy, combining live performance with candid conversation. Following his set, we'll welcome Chloe Radcliffe to join him for an unfiltered, behind-the-scenes discussion about the art of stand-up, the craft of comedy, the inspiration behind the jokes, and the ever-evolving landscape of comedy in the digital age. Join us for an unforgettable blend of laughter and learning that showcases the power of comedy to connect, provoke thought, and entertain.

events.title: Where Data Meets Creativity: Making Brave Brand Calls
events.description:
In an era of dashboards, real-time metrics, and predictive analytics, it’s easy to mistake data for direction. But transformative brand moments don’t come from simply following what the numbers say; they come from leaders who interpret data through an informed and insightful lens — who see patterns others miss, ask better questions, and make bold decisions that single data points alone would never justify. This panel explores how modern CMOs use data not as a safety net, but as a springboard. 

Join us for a conversation with marketing visionaries — John Livanos, Krista Dalton, Eric Liedtke and Clayton Ruebensaal — who have leveraged data for creative advantage.

speakers.name: Eric Liedtke
speakers.title: Chief Marketing Officer & Evp, Strategy At Under Armour And Co-Founder Of Unless

speakers.name: Clayton Ruebensaal
speakers.title: Cmo
speakers.company: Ex American Express, The Ritz-Carlton, Comcast NBCUuniversal

events.title: Will your job still exist in five years?
events.description: AI is remaking the labor market at breakneck speed. Futurist and Singularity University guest lecturer Michelle Schneider poses the question haunting every professional: Will your job still exist in five years? Blending cutting‑edge research with real‑world stories, she offers a four‑pillar survival kit—innovative mindset, tech literacy, emotional intelligence, mental health—empowering you to turn uncertainty into strategic advantage.

events.title: The Writers Room LIVE
events.description: A behind-the-scenes look inside a real comedy writers’ room with Seth Green, his Robot Chicken co-creator, and his writing team. Watch as they break stories, chase punch lines, and riff in real time onstage, using Superhuman as a creative collaborator.

events.title: Amy Gallo Book Signing
events.description: Amy Gallo will be signing copies of “Getting Along” at the SXSW Bookstore.

events.title: Any1 Brand Showcase & Tasting at SXSW
events.description:
Discover a Japanese plant-based food brand featuring chocolate, ice cream, and tofu.

Sample Any1 Choco and Any1 Tofu and explore the future potential of plant-based foods in the U.S. market.

events.title: Dreamina AI Meetup
events.description:
Join AI creators, filmmakers, visual artists and industry visionaries at this meetup. We’ll dive into the future of AI-powered content creation and collaborative innovation, exchange ideas, find partners, draw inspiration from cutting-edge workflows, and build meaningful connections to fuel new creative paths.

For more information, please visit: https://luma.com/cxt01tse

events.title: Film & TV Industry Happy Hour
events.description: Lights. Camera. Happy Hour! Join Wrapbook at our SXSW Film & TV Industry Happy Hour. We are bringing the film and television community together for an evening of great drinks, fresh introductions, and future collaborations. Come meet the people behind the productions, expand your circle, and spark the kinds of conversations that turn into your next project.

events.title: Staying Alive with Jon Gabrus & Adam Pally
events.description: Jon Gabrus & Adam Pally are hitting SXSW with a special LIVE episode of their SmartLess Media podcast, Staying Alive. The two 40 something year-old friends are following up their TV series, "101 Places to Party Before You Die", with a comedic look at wellness, health & life improvement. Find out what Pally & Gabrus and their special guests do to Stay Alive.

events.title: Tennessee House - Nashville at Night
events.description:
The Tennessee House showcases what's happening in tech, innovation, and culture across the Volunteer State. Be there for 3 days of bold thinking, eye-opening connections, and unforgettable fun.

We're spotlighting Nashville from 5pm to 11pm. Add a dash of hot chicken heat at the sweet spot where innovation meets creativity… Plus, Hip Hop Karaoke and late-night line dancing for Dolly Parton's 80th birthday.

Doors open at 5pm ** Limited-edition swag, bites, and drinks **

events.title: Matt McElvogue’s happy hour lightning talk
events.description:
Join us for Happy Hour with Teague VP of Design Matt McElvogue. He’s sharing about designing for shared autonomy – an essential next step as we collaborate with machines.

Machines are no longer just tools. They are teammates. But can we trust them? Join Teague VP of Design, Matt McElvogue, for a happy hour lightning talk about designing for the shift from direct control to shared autonomy. Designing for emergence will shape the next era of human-machine collaboration. What does it take to design emergence we can trust?

events.title: The Peril at Pincer Point
events.description: Jim Baitte, a layabout sound designer desperate to prove himself, is working on a new horror flick from the tyrannical yet lauded b-movie director P.W. Griffin. Accused of lacking vision and creative courage, Jim is sent to the remote island where the film was shot to capture a sound powerful enough to elevate the film's finale. Once there, eerie local fables surface: for years, ambitious and headstrong youth have lost their souls to a ghostly sea captain for his spectral crew. As Jim entangles himself further into the bizarre locals, scenery, and prophecy, he can’t help but ponder the ever-confirming legend, and if recording it might just cost him more than his career.

events.title: Ceremony
events.description: When the ooligan vanishes from Bella Coola, its absence remains like a scar, pointing to a history that reaches far beyond the river. From ramshackled Nuxalk Radio, voices rise through crackling airwaves to trace the forces no one was meant to uncover. What begins as a local broadcast becomes an awakening as testimony, watercolour animation and rare archival weave a story of survival, return and the quiet revolution of an Indigenous Nation that refuses to disappear.

events.title: Launching OH.io: Performance Venture
events.description: Join us at SXSW for the launch of OH.io, a new kind of performance venture for founders with traction who are ready to scale. Instead of burning months and millions trying to go to market alone, OH.io takes on the cost, risk, and operational burden of building a revenue engine that actually scales, without touching a dollar of runway. Founders stay focused on the product, while we build and operate the GTM motion alongside them. OH.io combines an embedded GTM engine, a dedicated fund, a global event, and a physical operating hub called The Grid.Come meet the team on what it really takes to scale.

events.title: Over Your Dead Body
events.description: A dysfunctional couple head to a remote cabin to supposedly reconnect, but each has secret plans to kill the other.

events.title: Their Town
events.description: When Abby’s boyfriend drops out of the high school play, she finds herself helping a school outlier step into the role opposite her. They spend a long night wandering around their town, examining their futures and unearthing surprises from their past.

events.title: And Her Body Was Never Found
events.description: Mor Cohen and Polaris Banks did the impossible, made a movie with just two people, while camping, with a script based on their real arguments. Most couples would kill each other under those conditions. They were no exception.

events.title: Animated Short Program
events.description: A whirlwind tour of hand drawn, stop-motion, and digital revelries.
events.venue: Rollins Theatre at the Long Center

events.title: Sender
events.description: Julia was fired three weeks ago. She also got sober three weeks ago. She’s starting over in a suburban rental, and doing a lot of online shopping to help make the space her own, fast. When packages she didn’t order start showing up at her door — a blender, a corkscrew, her signature shade of lipstick — they feel so unnervingly tied to her past that it starts to feel like someone is watching her. The shopping site Smirk denies responsibility. But increasingly paranoid, Julia tumbles down a rabbit hole to find the identity of her anonymous sender.

events.title: The Stand Comedy Club Presents: 10 for 10 Podcast Live at SXSW
events.description: The Stand brings its acclaimed 10 for 10 podcast of record to life on stage at SXSW, turning intimate, no-holds-barred conversations into an unforgettable live experience. 10 for 10 is The Stand's signature series celebrates a decade (and counting) of the club's raw, transformative impact on stand-up comedy. Each episode dives deep with a standout comedian who calls The Stand home- unpacking the grind, the bombs, the breakthroughs, the green-room chaos, and the nights that changed everything. Past guests include Jim Gaffigan, Shane Gillis, Ari Shaffir, Janeane Garofalo, T.J. Miller and more!

events.title: Stories We Tell: Women + Gender Diverse Filmmakers
events.description: Explore the nuts and bolts of getting a film funded and made in this discussion highlighting Film Fatales members who directed features premiering at SXSW including Jennifer Holness (#WhileBlack), Jo Rochelle (Dead Deer High), and Luchina Fisher (The Dads). Moderated by Brit Fryer (Adam’s Apple). Learn about their creative and professional journeys in this dynamic conversation with filmmakers pushing the boundaries of cinema. Followed by a networking reception celebrating filmmakers of all marginalized genders.

events.title: Your Attention Please
events.description:
A new generation of parents, teens, and reformers are fighting back against Big Tech’s agenda to define the future of human connection. From Kristin, a mother pursuing legislative reform after losing her son, to Trisha, a young programmer building technology to stop cyberbullying, the film reveals how deeply the attention economy is reshaping us.

Blending intimate human stories with insights from leading experts in tech reform and digital wellbeing, "Your Attention Please" asks some of the most urgent questions of our time: Can we reclaim our autonomy? Can technology be redesigned to serve humanity? And what does a healthier relationship with the digital world look like for us and our kids?

events.title: Big Girls Don't Cry
events.description: Summer 2006, 14-year-old Sid is caught between her own burgeoning sexual curiosity and acceptance from an older group of girls. As she delves deeper into rebellion, she leaves behind a trail of destruction as she goes. Big Girls Don’t Cry is a love letter to all the women that still feel shame scars from this time of their lives; who did things they wished they hadn’t, or didn’t do things they wished they had; to hold up a mirror and say yes; that was f#&*ed up.

events.title: Music Video Program
events.description: A dynamic mix of creativity and stylish visuals where music and storytelling collide.

events.title: SXSW Pitch Award Ceremony
events.description: On Friday, March 13, and Saturday, March 14, the 2026 SXSW Pitch will feature 45 innovative technology companies across nine categories: Enterprise and Future of Work; Entertainment, Media, Sports & Creator Content; Healthcare, AssistiveTech & BioTech; Innovative World Tech; Intelligent Systems, Robotics & Multisensory Technology; Smart Cities, Transportation, Manufacturing & Logistics; Smart Data, Security & FinTech; Student Startups; and Sustainability, AgTech & Food.Join us at 6:30 PM to discover the winner in each category, along with several special awards.

events.title: Agridulce (Bittersweet)
events.description:
In the Dominican town of Cabarete, bachata is a way of life far from the dance halls that it occupies overseas. A snapshot of four children, each confronting an existential challenge, Agridulce shows how music guides their journey of self discovery. With five years of filming, director Frank Pavich (Jodorowsky’s Dune) captures pivotal moments of the children’s coming of age.

Generations collide, and the children struggle for balance in a world troubled by conflict. Along the way, they’re mentored by teachers of a school devoted to bachata, the once denigrated music that has become the Dominican Republic’s primary cultural export.

events.title: Don't Tell Comedy All Stars in partnership with Deadline
events.description: As part of SXSW, Deadline is partnering with Don’t Tell Comedy for a special edition of Don’t Tell Comedy All Stars, set to take place Saturday, March 14 at The Creek and The Cave in Austin, TX. The evening will feature a live comedy showcase performed by five standout alumni from Don’t Tell Comedy’s acclaimed Secret Sets Series, spotlighting some of the most exciting voices working in stand-up today. Lineup coming soon!

events.title: Lucaa
events.description:
Originally from the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina but currently living between LA, NYC and Richmond, VA; Lucaa (she/they) is the brainchild of singer/producer Stepha, who is a 2 spirit Afro-Indigenous artist whose genre-bending indie/alt-pop brand of music features raw and deceptively deep songwriting that pulls from their experiences as a young model in NYC, and being a queer BIPOC artist.  

At a young age, Lucaa remembers listening to their father (who was a backup singer for Stevie Wonder, Earth Wind and Fire, and Michael Jackson) and mother (a trained opera singer). After teaching themself how to sing and play songs on piano by ear, Lucaa now takes a grungier approach to altpop, with influences harnessed from Radiohead, Billie Eilish, Willow, & girl in red.

Lucaa's career is growing quickly. A notable SXSW 2024 showcase early on led to major label interest and a fruitful year of performances and international branding campaigns with Leica Cameras and TurboTax. Lucaa was also a featured artist alongside Black Eyed Peas front man Taboo for Reserved Magazine, and appeared in Vogue Japan's October Edition (print), KEXP, Ones to Watch, and Them.

events.title: Obsession
events.description: After breaking the mysterious “One Wish Willow” to win his crush’s heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for but soon discovers that some desires come at a dark, sinister price.

events.title: Redbreast Unhidden Bar
events.description:
The Redbreast Unhidden Bar is back for its second year! On March 13 - 14, step into the exclusive world of Redbreast Single Pot Still Irish Whiskey, where guests can discover expertly crafted cocktails and tastings with a cinematic twist.

Attendees must be over 21, be SXSW badge holders, and have pre-registered their attendance at the link below. Entry is also not guaranteed and permitted on a first come first serve basis.

Pre-register here: https://url.uk.m.mimecastprotect.com/s/Mn7eCL4NfREzGxhPi7Iyl7Et?domain=redbreastwhiskey.com

events.title: A Safe Distance
events.description: Alex and her boyfriend Joey head into the wilderness for a romantic getaway. When Alex turns down Joey's surprise proposal, he abandons her in the woods. She’s rescued by Kianna and Matt, an enigmatic young couple living off the grid. Stranded and shaken, Alex accepts their invitation to stay at their remote campsite. As she’s drawn into their intoxicating world, complicated emotions and unexpected connections begin to surface. But when she learns they’re fugitives wanted for a string of violent bank robberies, Alex must navigate the blurred lines between desire, loyalty, and survival.
