events.title: The Moth & the Gates Foundation Present: Mothers of Invention
events.description:
The Moth and the Gates Foundation present an afternoon of true stories exploring the health of women around the world. Hosted by stand-up comedian, writer, and actress, Ivy Le, with opening remarks by author of Four Mothers, Abigail Leonard, and music by Austin violinist, Steele, this program features three global storytellers, whose experiences will spark conversation about care, culture, and the changing realities of women’s health.

4:00p - Doors open with drinks reception
4:30p - 5:45p - Show + Discussion
5:45p - 6:30p - Post show reception with food from La Pera

events.title: Music Managers Forum Meet-Up
events.description: Meet the Managers is a must-attend gathering for music managers at SXSW, whether you’re a seasoned industry veteran or just starting out. Hosted by Music Managers Forum-US (MMF-US), the leading trade association for music managers in the U.S. and a proud member of the IMMF global network, this event brings together managers from around the world to connect, exchange insights, and discuss key issues shaping the business of artist management. MMF-US executives and board members will be on hand to share updates on advocacy, membership, and initiatives, and to connect with the global manager community.

speakers.name: Wesley T. A'Harrah
speakers.title: VP of Membership & Education at Music Managers Forum-US (MMF-US) and Partner & Portfolio CMO of Orange Reign GP

events.title: Renaissance in Obesity Treatment Innovation
events.description: Given the need for effective obesity treatments and the limits of current GLP-1 receptor agonists, such as muscle loss, poor tolerability, and frequent dosing, a next-generation solution is essential. Ideal treatments would focus on fat loss and muscle preservation, offer strong safety and tolerability, and be dosed less frequently. Advancements in RNA medicines, growth of human genetics databases, and potential for combination therapies have opened the door for innovative new therapies and combination approaches. Explore expert insights on future treatment opportunities.

events.title: Round Table: Publicity and Marketing: Annie Jeeves, Justin Solar, and Danielle McCarthy-Boles
events.description: An extension of our popular Mentor Sessions, our Round Table Sessions not only allow attendees to learn from the industry experts that sit at each of the three tables in this session but they also allow attendees to learn from the questions and experiences of their peers as well. This Round Table Session will bring together industry experts and SXSW attendees for an enlightening discussion on Publicity and Marketing.

events.title: Sex in Outer Space & the Researchers Making It Happen (Soon)
events.description: Building on a 2023 SXSW presentation, this panel will be a light-hearted but highly educational conversation on the current science focusing on past, present, and future questions around human sexual activity in outer space environments - whether on private commercial space stations of the near future, or settlements on the surface of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Panelists will include some of the world's leading recognized experts in this fascinating and highly specific research field, covering everything from space medicine and biological reproduction to psychosocial issues and crew dynamics.

speakers.title: Astronaut, Physician, Director, Chief of Space Medicine

events.title: Sober Space Meet Up - 3/17
events.description: Sober Space is a welcoming gathering place for people in all forms of recovery during SXSW 2026. This space hosts all-format recovery meetings for Friends of Bill and all SXSW attendees who are seeking a supportive meeting environment during the festival. Participants are invited to sit together and share experience, strength, and hope in a confidential, judgment-free setting. Meetings are facilitated by The SIMS Foundation alongside trusted leaders from the recovery community.

events.title: SpectreVision Radio Live: CHILDHOOD’S END: SPECULATION ON A POST-DISCLOSURE WORLD
events.description:
What happens to civilization when the extraordinary is no longer theoretical?
Last year’s documentary Age of Disclosure awakened millions to the reality that UFOs and non-human intelligence may be genuine phenomena, reframing the conversation from fringe belief to serious public inquiry. Constitutional attorney and prominent disclosure advocate Danny Sheehan takes the next step, examining the legal, cultural, and spiritual ramifications of a post-disclosure world. What shifts when the fantastic becomes fact? How do governments, institutions, religions, and markets adapt? And how does human identity evolve when we are no longer alone? Moderated by SpectreVision Radio Director Daniel Noah.

events.title: Unlocking Africa: Real Partnerships and Real Results
events.description: Africas music market is one of the fastest-growing and most dynamic in the world but success depends on more than a viral hit. In this session we’ll unpack the strategies behind breaking artists across the continent and beyond. From navigating fragmented streaming platforms and hyper-local radio to street teams, fan communities, and brand collabs, you’ll hear what works, what flops and what it takes to build lasting careers in Africa’s diverse music scenes. Expect a real case study of how one artist cracked the local market and the roadmap that turned regional buzz into international momentum.

events.title: UX / AX Designers and Researchers Meet Up
events.description: Connect with a global community of UX and AX designers and researchers shaping the future of digital experiences. Hosted by Cindy Brummer of Standard Beagle and UX in ATX, this popular meetup returns to SXSW to bring together creatives working across user-centered design and AI-enabled experiences. Whether you’re into product design, research, or agentic systems, join us to swap ideas, network, and get inspired. All experience levels welcome—come meet your people!

events.title: Why Indies Still Matter: Independent Music & Consolidation
events.description: The recorded music industry is becoming more consolidated, with major labels acquiring independent music organizations at a faster clip, and the role of the independent sector is shifting as a result. UMG’s proposed acquisition of Downtown Music Holdings is just one example of this, though the trend has been increasing in recent years. In this changing landscape, what does independent music mean in 2026, and is it still important? What resources and strategies can independent artists use to build their careers as the industry continues to evolve?

events.title: Mark Roberge Book Signing
events.description: Mark Roberge will be signing copies of “The Science of Scaling” at the SXSW Bookstore.

events.title: Karma Sheen
events.description:
Karma Sheen is a London-based project led by British-Pakistani artist Sameer Khan, fusing the spirit of psychedelic rock with the emotional depth of Hindustani Classical music. Born from the tension between tradition and distortion, the project reimagines raag-based forms through fuzz pedals, improvisation and diasporic imagination.
Rooted in Khan’s training under Ustaad Latafat Ali Khan (Sham Chaurasi Gharana), Karma Sheen translates classical ornamentation into immersive soundscapes. Khan is joined by guitarist Amad Chima, sitarist Rodrigo Bourganos, bassist and visual artist Grisha Grebbenikov, and drummer/DJ Arun Dhanjal, forming a collaboration that bridges ancient lineage with contemporary subculture.
The band released their debut album in 2023, followed by extensive UK and European touring, including sold-out headline shows at Rich Mix and the 100 Club, and festival appearances at Shambala and Trans Musicales, where they recorded a KEXP live session due for release in early 2026.
Now working with EBB Music, Karma Sheen are building international momentum as they prepare to release their second album in 2026.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth Patio

events.title: Film & TV Industry Happy Hour
events.description: Join us for the Film in Tulsa Filmmaker Happy Hour, presented by the Tulsa Office of Film, Music, Arts & Culture, Cherokee Film, New York University, and Creative Equity Initiative.Mix and mingle with film commissioners, filmmakers, and industry creatives. Learn more about Northeast Oklahoma’s booming production scene — from the state-of-the-art Cherokee Film Studios to local and state incentives.Whether you’re scouting your next location, or just here for a great conversation, we look forward to seeing you there.

events.title: Campeón Gabacho
events.description: Campeón Gabacho tells the story of Liborio, an endearing and mischievous young migrant whose only talent is taking punches. He crosses the Rio Grande to escape a harsh reality in Mexico, looking for a better life in the United States, and settles in a Latino barrio in New York City. Through his fists, his love, and his words, he faces cultural walls and prejudices that threaten his hopes, and becomes a hero in an unknown land.

events.title: Danny Morel Book Signing
events.description: Danny Morel will be signing copies of “Awaken Your Highest Self” at the SXSW Bookstore.

events.title: Serling
events.description: "Serling" is an immersive first-person journey exploring the life and legacy of one of television’s most visionary storytellers, Rod Serling. Told almost entirely in Serling’s own words, drawn from never-before-heard recordings and personal dictations, the film captures the man behind "The Twilight Zone" in all his complexity. The film weaves archival material with atmospheric recreations that echo the eerie visual language Serling made iconic. As his unmistakable voice guides us, Serling emerges not only as a master of storytelling, but as a man grappling with the trauma of war, the moral compromises of fame, and the hope that America might one day live up to its own ideals.

events.title: Their Town
events.description: When Abby’s boyfriend drops out of the high school play, she finds herself helping a school outlier step into the role opposite her. They spend a long night wandering around their town, examining their futures and unearthing surprises from their past.

events.title: The Way We Move
events.description: THE WAY WE MOVE is a feature-length documentary about Amber Galloway, a star ASL (American Sign Language) interpreter who specializes in live music interpretations. Amber teaches her art to share her life’s mission : making music accessible to the Deaf community. Armed with her astounding teaching skills, she will take her struggling new recruits on a one-of-a-kind journey, hoping they have what it takes to join her at Austin City Limits music festival. As the film unfolds, we learn about Amber’s painful past and about the lives of her recruits, Julian Ortiz and Angela "AV" Vilavong, as they come together and forge life-long bonds. A film about music, Deaf culture, connection and resilience.

events.title: Chasing Summer
events.description: After losing both her job and boyfriend, Jamie retreats to her small Texas hometown where friends and flings from a fateful high school summer turn her life upside down.

events.description: Authentic storytelling that captivates, surprises, and excites!

events.title: Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story
events.description: Blurring the line between performance and personal crisis, comedian Maria Bamford turns her mental health journey into material that’s riotously funny and ultimately inspiring. What emerges is a portrait of an artist transforming vulnerability into creative strength through honesty.

events.title: Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story

events.title: Scarlet Girls
events.description: What does it mean to be a woman in a country where abortion is banned in all circumstances? In this lyrical documentary, women and girls speak about the challenges and consequences regarding unsafe abortion in the Dominican Republic.

events.title: Unlocking Her Next Chapter | Fertility with Dr. Molly Maloof, MD
events.description: Day 2, Dr. Molly Maloof explores the core biological imperatives that drive human behavior—and whether they align or conflict with longevity. This fireside chat expands the concept of reproduction beyond biology, examining how the drive to create shows up in relationships, art, technology, and legacy, often shaping choices unconsciously. Dr. Maloof will discuss the grandmother paradox, fertility as a signal of system-wide health, and the critical role of relationships and social bonds in lifespan and healthspan. Attendees will walk away with a new perspective on fertility, purpose, and connection—along with exclusive custom content and a book signing designed to deepen these insights beyond the event. Dr. Maloof is a physician, author, educator, and visionary committed to radically extending human healthspan and unleashing human potential.

events.title: We Are The Shaggs
events.description: Three sisters from rural New Hampshire formed a band in the late 1960s, but not by choice. Betty, Dorothy, and Helen Wiggin had no interest in playing music. In fact, they had no musical abilities at all. It was their father Austin, inspired by a prophecy, who became convinced that his girls would become rock stars. He pulled his daughters out of school, bought them a pair of cheap guitars and a drum kit, dubbed them The Shaggs, and basically commanded them to make music. In 1969, he brought the girls to a storefront recording studio outside of Boston, and the result is one of the most head-scratching and polarizing albums ever committed to vinyl. "We Are The Shaggs" is their story.

events.title: Seekers of Infinite Love
events.description:
Kayla Bachman, an author who struggles with emotional connection, Zach Bachman, a lawyer who dreams of being a folk singer and Wes Bachman, a graphic novelist / gambling & pill addict, meet to discuss their younger sister Scarlett who joined a cult in Kentucky. 
Zach and his dysfunctional and absent parents have hired cult deprogrammer Rick Delacroix to help them rescue Scarlett. 
They embark on a roadtrip to save their sister, and bring their family together.

events.title: The Dads
events.description: Inspired by the Emmy-Award winning short documentary of the same name (Netflix, 2023), "The Dads" chronicles fathers of trans and nonbinary children as they are forced to choose between country and family when a new right-wing administration and conservative Supreme Court take hold in the United States. Filmed over the course of a year spanning retreats in rural Maine and Minnesota, protests, family milestones, a pivotal U.S. Supreme Court decision, and the collapse of gender-affirming care for youth, "The Dads" captures this national reckoning with remarkable intimacy through verite footage and interviews with the film’s main protagonists. This is fatherhood as an act of radical resistance.

events.title: Hokum
events.description: When novelist Ohm Bauman retreats to a remote inn to scatter his parents’ ashes, he is consumed by tales of a witch haunting the honeymoon suite. Disturbing visions and a shocking disappearance forces him to confront dark corners of his past.

events.title: Kill Me
events.description: Jimmy wakes up in a bathtub filled with his own blood, his wrists slit and his life rapidly nearly completion. This would be a textbook failed suicide attempt, only…Jimmy didn’t do it? At least, he’s pretty sure he didn’t. Alongside Margot, the 911 operator who took his call that faithful night, Jimmy begins an amateur-hour murder investigation, desperate to prove that this is a whodunnit and not a hedunnit. The list of suspects who might be happy if Jimmy wasn’t around anymore is fairly long—angry ex-girlfriends, frustrated siblings, exasperated psychiatrists, and resentful stepfathers. But the prime suspect is Jimmy himself.

events.title: Obsession
events.description: After breaking the mysterious “One Wish Willow” to win his crush’s heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for but soon discovers that some desires come at a dark, sinister price.

events.title: Ananto
events.description:
Ananto is a multifaceted saxophonist, singer, and rapper whose sound lives at the intersection of heritage and modern expression. Drawing from his Indian roots and deep influences in jazz and R&B, Ananto creates music that feels both timeless and forward-thinking.

Rooted in improvisation and groove, his saxophone work carries the emotional depth of jazz while his vocals and rap bring a contemporary edge shaped by soul, rhythm, and storytelling. Ananto seamlessly blends melodic phrasing with rhythmic flow, crafting performances that move fluidly between genres without losing authenticity.

Inspired by the richness of Indian musical identity and the expressive freedom of jazz and R&B, Ananto’s artistry is a celebration of cultural fusion. Whether on stage or in the studio, he uses music as a bridge—connecting tradition and innovation, discipline and spontaneity, sound and story.

With a distinct voice and an ever-evolving sound, Ananto represents a new generation of artists unafraid to honor their roots while redefining the boundaries of modern music.

events.title: J-Nice The Kingdom Builder
events.description:
J-Nice The Kingdom Builder, is an Austin, TX Christian hip-hop artist who has been creating music for over 20 years. He is the founder of Kingdom Builder Ministries. This movement inspires youth and young adults to use the arts to present the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

J-Nice has released seven Mixtapes, over 20 Music Videos, published poems, hosted the longest-running Christian hip-hop showcase in the state of Texas, won Christian Hip-Hop Artist of the Year at the Kingdom Excellence Awards, and released 4  albums that have charted on Apple Music. He has been on platforms presented by the National Football League, MTV, BET, CBS, Spectrum News, and many more.  This lyrical wordsmith makes it his duty to teach biblical truths with witty and clever wordplay, which is sure to leave listeners pleasantly surprised.

events.title: Junerise
events.description:
"Bruce Springsteen + Cocteau Twins = Junerise" - KUTX

Junerise is the heartland dream pop project of Austin-based, Utah-transplant singer-songwriter June Bennion, (They/Them).

Looking ever skyward, June channels influences from the grounding story-centric songwriting chops of James Taylor and Bruce Springsteen to the ethereal gradient-scapes of The Cocteau Twins and Brian Eno with a dash of The Cure's dance-forward sensibilities. Their songwriting comes from a well of lived experiences growing up as a closeted queer person in the god-fearing Mormon mountain states.

June tackles feelings of isolation, wonder, and perseverance against the odds set against a sunset sky, quickly fading out of view as each song flows from scene to scene as each story is told. Junerise is a long incubated project which at times is downright danceable while also reveling in the beautiful transience of each passing moment.

events.title: Ruido Selecto
events.description: Ruido Selecto is a musician, producer, and sound engineer from Medellín, Colombia. His music focuses on Caribbean rhythms such as Cumbia, Salsa, Electronic Dub, and Afro-diasporic styles that have traditionally reached Colombia through the Picó Soundsystem culture. Ruido defines his sound as "Caribbean Bass." Since 2015, he has released two studio albums and several collaborations and EPs (Secret Lab 2015, Piratería Caribeña y Contrabando 2019 Equador 2022, and Cumbia Soundsystem EP 2025). In 2024, he released a series of remixes of iconic tracks from the legendary Colombian label Discos Fuentes, titled 14 CAÑONAZOS EN DUB, an audiovisual production that was highlighted by the specialized media outlet Gladys Palmera. He has toured nationally and internationally in Mexico and Central America, with additional performances in the United States and Europe. Ruido Selecto has participated in festivals such as Altavoz, África Futura, and Invazion Fest, sharing the stage with artists like Mitú, Afrotronix, Ghetto Kumbé, Systema Solar, Alligatorz, among others. He has worked as a producer and mastering engineer for Discos Fuentes , Folcore Barcelona and No Sabes.

events.title: Tokyo Joshi Pro Wrestling TEXAS STAMPEDE -March 2026
events.description:
For the first time ever, Tokyo Joshi Pro Wrestling arrives in Austin — and makes its SXSW debut. TJPW Texas Stampede is a high-energy tri-city tour across Austin, Dallas, and Houston, featuring 18 star wrestlers from Tokyo Joshi Pro Wrestling, Japan’s premier all-women’s promotion — marking one of the largest international showcases in women’s pro-wrestling history.

Driven by the motto “Kawaii × Dream × Strong,” TJPW delivers a one-of-a-kind entertainment experience where pop-idol charm meets world-class athleticism. Nowhere else will you see a performer singing to the crowd one moment and launching a perfectly timed dropkick the next.

This super-happy, family-friendly cultural event welcomes fans of all ages — bring your friends, bring your kids, and experience the excitement together. At TJPW, All Women Are Heroes.

events.title: Deloyd Elze
events.description: Deloyd Elze, aka Jacob Henry Allen, is a genre-blending artist and poet from Jacksonville, Florida, whose music fuses traditional American songwriting with experimental and electronic textures. Over the past decade, Deloyd has tinkered with soundscapes that meld twangy guitars, lo-fi drums, dissonant synths and rich acoustic textures into ‘digital twang,’ a sound that seamlessly weaves between country, indie and electronic. The name Deloyd Elze honors his great-grandfather, a resilient man whose legacy of grit and defiance inspires his artistry. Like his namesake, Deloyd’s music is rooted in authenticity, reflecting the complexities of the human experience. Now based in Los Angeles, he’s creating music that speaks to life’s many layers, drawing from his family’s history and his own journey of self-discovery and survival.

events.title: Dropout Improv
events.description: The highly popular comedy platform takes its sharp wit and quick-thinking comedy offline and onto the stage in a special SXSW performance! Dropout have been running their subscription comedy platform since 2018 and have tailored their improv skills for a live audience, promising a hilarious night of games and absurdity.Dropout was born out of the hugely successful comedy website College Humor and produces a wide variety of shows in a completely independent setting. They have quickly amassed a large audience through titles like Dimension 20,  Game Changer, Very Important People and more, utilizing formats that mix razor-sharp comedy with gameplay. In this show hosted by Kurt Maloney, all of those finely crafted skills will be on show in a night of varied games and freewheeling comedy. Things are about to get wild. Reservations are available for 300 Platinum Badgeholders through SXSW GO or on the web schedule. Arrive 30 minutes prior to the event to pick up a ticket at will call.
events.venue: Austin City Limits Live at the Moody Theater

events.title: Blakchyl
events.description:
Rapper Blakchyl's (formerly known as T-Fly) is a talented, community-minded wordsmith, having come up in the local hip hop community collaborating with music collectives, nonprofits and filmmakers. The queer artist has three European tours under her belt plus opening slots for Talib Kweli, Snow Tha Product, Jean Grae, Bizzy Bone and Scarface and her new album Better Than I Imagined (produced by The Mask), was accompanied by a short film and dropped in July. Always indefatigable, she recently landed a deal with Brighton, UK-based Tru Thought Records as well as an Austin Chronicle cover, was nominated for Best Hip Hop Artist, released an EP (Call Me Sometimes) and played a Waterloo Records in-store. It all comes down to her
"powerful and effervescent songs" (CultureMap) and her love for the craft and it's community.

events.title: DJ Candlestick
events.description:
DJ Candlestick has seen success throughout the music industry as a member of The Nice Guys, and then the Chopstars.
Starting his career as a young teenager Candlestick built his name up during his high school years and at University Of Houston. While there he was also a founding member of the Nice Guys. As a member of The Chopstars, he is the Founder of ChopCares.

His DJ skill has reached far beyond Houston as he’s been featured on programs such as the Ebro Show on Apple Music, as well as a Black Music Monday mix for Apple Music, NTS live (UK), was a former mixer with 93.7 The Beat , 90.9 KTSU (his alma mater) & Sound 42 on Sirius Xm radio. His work has also been featured in the Oscar Award Winning film Moonlight directed by Barry Jenkins, who he’s also collaborated with on “Purple Moonlight” as well as “If Beale Street Was Chopped” He also has Official Album remixes with Drake, Brent Faiyaz, Thundercat, Don Toliver , Metro Boomin , Little Dragon , Dvsn , Partynextdoor and more. Candlestick also was featured on Mo Amer’s Netflix special “The Vagabond”  and has been a feature DJ at Coachella, Billboard and Redbull events as well as opening up for Dave Chappelle

events.title: Atsuko Chiba
events.description: Montréal’s Atsuko Chiba offer “pounding, angular rock” (BrooklynVegan), venturesomely crossing genre-defining borders with a cohesive and hypnotic blend of post-rock, progressive rock, and krautrock, weaving together a rich sonic tapestry that subverts through offbeat songwriting. In concert, they combine their unique brand of experimental rock with video and light installations triggered in real time by the band. While touring Canada, the United States, Europe, and the United Kingdom with their telepathic audiovisual tempest, the outfit have shared the stage with the likes of ...And You Will Know Us by the Trail of Dead, Big Business, King Buffalo, and Duchess Says, also playing notable events such as Portals Festival, SXSW, and M for Montreal. Since 2013, they have released three full-length albums (Jinn, Trace, and Water, It Feels Like It’s Growing), two EPs (Figure and Ground and The Memory Empire), as well as a slew of singles. After offering booming tracks “Pope’s Cocaine” and “Climax Therapy” in the Summer of 2025, the five-piece unveil Atsuko Chiba on April 24th, 2026 via Mothland.

events.title: Jasmine Jethwa
events.description:
Jasmine makes swaying, folk-tinged acoustic pop songs with a full voice that teems with rich emotion. Her sonic palette makes sense when she describes the music she was most interested in growing up. “The earliest memories I have are of driving down to see my grandparents, and we listened to different music in the car on my dad’s iPod,” she recalls, “There’d be David Gray, Tracy Chapman, Dido, Gipsy Kings, The Eagles – old songs, classic albums. And I feel like they went into my psyche. I’m obsessed with any kind of acoustic, well-played guitar.”

She also references her love of R&B and a current new love with Fontaines DC (“the first time I heard them they grabbed my heart; if my music does what they and other artists do for me and moves them to feel something, I’d be happy”). There is also mention of the emotional resonance of watching Bollywood films with her Gujarati grandmother back when she was a kid: “In terms of vocals, I do think that’s made a bit of an impact,” she says of those Hindi songs she internalised.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth

events.title: Jeff Akoh
events.description:
Jeff Akoh is a Nigerian singer-songwriter whose soulful vocals and genre-blending sound sit at the crossroads of Afropop and R&B. He rose to prominence as the youngest winner of MTN Project Fame West Africa, marking the beginning of a steadily evolving music career.

He has since released a growing body of work that has amassed millions of streams across digital platforms, anchored by his debut album Lokoja and a run of widely received singles. In 2025, Akoh released his latest EP, Rebel Heart, a project that reflects a more personal and boundary-pushing phase of his artistry.

Akoh has collaborated with a range of artists across genres, including Eric Bellinger, alongside other notable regional and international creatives, continuing to expand his sound and global reach.

events.title: Jovi Greene
events.description: Jovi Greene is an 18-year-old breakout country artist from Maryland with more than 7 million streams. He’s already opened for Jake Owen, Riley Green, Aaron Watson, Whiskey Myers, and more. Jovi has earned a loyal following through his cinematic, self-produced content and a performance style that turns first-time listeners into real fans.

events.title: Mega Ran
events.description:
Mega Ran (Raheem Jarbo) is a GRAMMY-nominated rapper, author, and former middle school teacher whose career proves hip-hop has no boundaries. A pioneer of nerdcore, he blends sharp lyricism with education, storytelling, and pop culture — drawing inspiration from video games, comics, and professional wrestling.

His music has been licensed by Capcom and featured in major video games (Mortal Kombat 11, TMNT: Shredder’s Revenge), television (WWE, AEW), and film (Clerks III). He’s toured internationally, performed at Madison Square Garden, and he's produced an EMMY winning musical.

In 2022, becoming a foster parent inspired Mega Ran to expand into family music. His children’s albums Buddy’s Magic Toy Box and Buddy’s Magic Tree House topped Billboard and iTunes charts, earned major playlist support, and led to a GRAMMY nomination for Best Children’s Album.

Known for high-energy, all-ages performances, Mega Ran is just as comfortable rocking libraries and museums as he is festivals and wrestling rings. Living up to his “Teacher / Rapper / Hero” mantra, his mission remains simple: entertain, educate, and create spaces where everyone feels welcome.

events.title: Saint Avangeline
events.description:
Saint Avangeline is an Atlanta-based independent artist, merging ethereal sounds with raw, unfiltered vocals, crafting a striking contrast that mirrors the depths of human emotion. Deeply rooted in her journey with mental health, domestic abuse, & growing up queer, her songs offer an honest exploration of inner turmoil, rage, hope, & resilience. 
Growing up with her head in a sketchbook & performing in various orchestras, and jazz bands, combined with her unique sound-to-color synesthesia known as Chromesthesia, Avangeline focuses on writing and creating from a color palette. Music is like painting, every sound is a different texture, color, and form. She also often listens to music in languages she doesn't understand, are made up or distorted, or that contain no words at all. She found that she could focus more deeply on the emotion embedded within the sound and she would often memorize entire orchestral scores and video game soundtracks as a child. 
Focusing on painting an image not only through words but through the very fiber of sound, her music strives to transcend the barriers of language and strike hearts in the way hers was.

events.title: Semisoft
events.description: Semisoft is a dreamy post-grunge trio hailing from Tacoma, Washington. Blending spacey, hypnotic textures with explosive riff-driven energy, their sound lands somewhere between Fuzz, PJ Harvey, and Natural Child. Following the release of their Greenway Records debut 7", the band is preparing to unveil their second EP on Den Tapes, the Seattle-based cassette label and community founded by Kay Redden. Looking ahead, Semisoft’s long-awaited full-length album is slated for release next year.

events.title: Spencer Thomas
events.description:
Atlanta-based artist Spencer Thomas returns with Cynical Vision, his third and most incisive album yet, out March 20, 2026. Wry and sardonic, the record balances humor and existential dread, blending retro synths, vintage drum machines, and fuzzed-out guitars into an intoxicating mix of analog and electronic sounds. Nods to Randy Newman, Lou Reed, Warren Zevon, and Tom Petty shine through as Thomas holds a mirror to modern life, delivering a whip-smart meditation on the absurdity and beauty of living and loving in the 21st century.

“In a lot of ways, it felt impossible for me to not write about this stuff,” Thomas says. “I leaned into what felt interesting and current and funny, and tried to make something visceral and honest.”

After releasing his 2019 solo debut Hangin’ Tough, he moved to Athens, GA in 2020 and joined indie rock band Futurebirds as their keyboardist. “It was a fantastic opportunity,” he explains, “but it kept me away from home and from my own music.” His 2024 sophomore album The Joke of Life earned rave reviews, and in 2025 he stepped away from Futurebirds to devote himself fully to creating Cynical Vision.

events.title: Girl Tones
events.description:
Girl Tones, of planet Earth, are a high-energy rock duo brought to life by two sisters named Kenzie and Laila. Both classically trained musicians, Kenzie transitioned from cello to guitar and Laila from piano to drums in an effort to electrify sentient beings from this galaxy to the next. Their debut releases were produced by Brad Shultz of Cage The Elephant and released via his label Parallel Vision in partnership with Big Loud Rock.
Their first offerings have earned the praise of Rolling Stone, VICE, Consequence, PAPER, NME, DORK and many others with Flaunt saying, “Their sound is fluid, and yet with each release, they evolve as a harmonious group, developing their unique sound as one.”
Girl Tones has toured with Cage The Elephant across the globe, as well as The Velveteers, hey, nothing. and Silversun Pickups in North America. Making their unignorable festival debut at Lollapalooza, Shaky Knees, Austin City Limits and more, Rolling Stone said, “While the White Stripes — their most obvious comparison — were about controlled energy, Girl Tones are proudly imperfect.”
As the band jumps into 2026, they have no shortage of new music and new tour dates up their sleeves.

events.title: Lola Kinsey
events.description:
At 20, Texas-based artist Lola Kinsey is stepping fully into her own, blending classic rock roots with a modern pop shimmer. Her debut EP Come of Age captures the messy in-between of growing up. Heartbreak, family tension, and the pressure of figuring out who you’re supposed to be versus who you actually are.

Inspired by icons like Stevie Nicks, Cher, and Linda Ronstadt, Lola builds songs around strong melodies, big feelings, and a genre-bending spirit that feels both timeless and current. Ask her what genre she makes and she’ll still say “Linda Ronstadt,” a wink to her love of fearless storytelling and emotional honesty.

Momentum continues to build: three tracks from her debut EP Come of Age have received radio play on KXT and 88.1 Indie, and she appeared as an official SXSW 2025 showcase artist. With a return to SXSW and a Jambaloo appearance in 2026, plus her debut album slated for release this year, Lola is ready to take over the world one disco at a time.

events.title: sir eddie c
events.description:
Sir Eddie C is designing the next era of hip-hop from the middle of America.

The St. Louis–based artist represents a new St. Louis: forward-facing, culturally fluent, and unwilling to wait for co-signs. He calls his music “regular people rap,” but what distinguishes him is scale of vision. Each release arrives as a fully realized world, complete with its own aesthetic system, narrative arc, live direction, and sold-out limited merch.

He doesn’t drop projects. He builds worlds.

Concepts unfold through alter egos, staged moments, and immersive performances that feel cinematic without losing emotional precision. Beyond his own catalog, his annual Sir Eddie C & Friends show has grown into a packed, independently produced homecoming concert, proof that his audience doesn’t just listen. They participate, invest, and return.

With a sharp pen, controlled visual language, and commanding stage presence, Sir Eddie C operates as a full-package artist and multidisciplinary brand architect. He’s not waiting to be discovered. He’s constructing something too intentional to ignore.

events.title: Mark Brown
events.description: Mark Brown is a very versatile artist with a sound of his own blending raw passion with infectious beats. He makes bold calculated decisions with his approach on every record that usually leaves listeners in awe. Born and raised on the Nawfside of Houston, Tx, gave Mark Brown his grit and determination. He was inspired by his older brother’s which lead him down the path of rapping. With a mix of pain, motivation, and complexed catchy hooks, Mark Brown creates music that resonates with both the streets and the mainstream. With new music dropping monthly and a growing fanbase, Mark Brown is poised to kill the game!

events.title: Wave Chapelle & NilexNile
events.description: Hip-hop artist’s from the north side of Milwaukee who grew up on the sounds of Soulful Midwest rap. Separately they put out a steady stream of music over the last 5 years and have performed at various music festivals including Summerfest, Mile of music, and SXSW. Recently they’ve come together to form a duo ahead of their new project in the works for 2026.

events.title: Q Tha Hero
events.description: Hailing from Long Beach, California, Q THA HERO is an alternative rapper driven by authenticity and fearless individuality. He began making music at 13, building a foundation of raw songwriting and expressive delivery that’s become his signature. Drawing inspiration from superheroes, film, and pop culture, his music feels both personal and cinematic—balancing real emotion with larger-than-life energy. Now based on the East Coast, Q THA HERO continues to evolve while holding onto the grit and character of his West Coast roots. Bold, unfiltered, and unapologetically himself, he’s carving out a lane that’s impossible to ignore

events.title: Ras Mundi
events.description:
Ras Mundi is an international reggae band from Austin, TX that incorporates elements of hip-hop and rock & roll creating a conscious message of culture and unity.  
Up from humble roots, Ras Mundi currently consists of nine members working together to create a massive sound to heal the soul and the nation.  
Their sound resonates vocal harmonies, heavy percussion, melodic keys, thick baselines, and trumpet… with lyrics chanting down the Babylon System and resurrecting the movement of Jah people!

Ras Mundi has shared the stage with reggae luminaries The Wailers featuring Junior Marvin, Third World, and Michael Black.  
Ras Mundi hopes to accomplish big ‘TINGS in 2026 that includes playing the SXSW Music Festival, as well as releasing a full-length album of original material.  One love.

events.title: MC Frontalot
events.description: World's 579th-greatest rapper. Progenitor of nerdcore hip-hop and still that subgenre's Final Boss. Celebrating year 20 on tour.

events.title: KOJ
events.description:
KOJ is the sound of defiance rising from Liverpool, UK: a working-class voice turned outward, loud enough to cut through the noise, resilient enough to remain unshaken, and connected enough to represent a frustrated generation.

Drawing from the raw British sub-cultural sounds of Grime, Rap and Punk, KOJ creates music that confronts power while rooted in relatability and everyday struggle. Revolutionary in spirit yet populist in appeal, his music is built to connect, move, and be felt collectively. At its core is courage - raw, direct lyricism exploring survival and defiance, darkness and light, pressure and pride.

KOJ showcased his lyrical authority on his acclaimed debut EP Villain With A Conscience, earning support from Clash, Wonderland, The Face, Apple Music and Amazon Music.
Live is where KOJ reaches another level. He doesn’t perform - he leads. From Boomtown to Radio 1 Big Weekend, Reeperbahn and SXSW, his shows become charged, communal moments where tension turns to release.

More than a catalogue, KOJ is building a movement through purpose-driven visuals, tech-led collaborations and his growing TRiBE community — “a man on a mission,” as The F-Word Magazine puts it.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth Patio

events.title: Mariae Cassandra
events.description:
Mariae Cassandra is an Australian singer songwriter from Perth, Western Australia, rapidly emerging as one of the country’s most compelling new voices. First capturing attention through her online songwriting videos and viral moments across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, Mariae’s ability to pair intimate storytelling with hook driven pop has resonated with a growing global audience.

In 2024, Mariae won triple j Unearthed High with her breakout single “MillIon Billion Trillion” - a heartfelt ode to friendship that showcased her knack for emotionally direct, timeless songwriting. The win marked a turning point, positioning Mariae as a standout new artist and accelerating her rise beyond digital platforms.

Throughout 2024-25, Mariae built strong momentum, touring nationally as support for WAFIA, Spacey Jane, The Buoys and boywithuke, signing to Select Music and her debut EP “Everything In my Backpocket” via AWAL. 

In 2025, Mariae warmed up main stages for Charli XCX and beabadoobee at Laneway Festival, was named one of Live Nation’s Ones To Watch and showcased at BIGSOUND and SXSW Sydney.

events.title: Bea Porges
events.description:
Blending together the sounds of indie pop and folk melodies, Bea Porges lives in her own lyrical world. Throughout the years, the 25 year old singer songwriter has been working her way through the scenes of Atlanta and Athens, GA, and billing with touring acts such as hey, nothing, Infinity Songs, and Trash Panda. Her songwriting has a penchant for detail and wit, creating images that feel simultaneously personal and nostalgic.

While her love for solo songwriting is at the core of her musical endeavors, Bea performs as a five piece, turning acoustic songs into powerful and danceable live show that compliments her truthful lyrics. 

Filled with electric guitar and sprinkled with the sounds of banjo and lap steel, Bea’s 2025 EP, “The Cure, The Cause, The Killer,” explores feelings of desire, longing, and letting go with nods to the artists and genres that inspire her most. Through her love for songwriting and creating a symphony of sound from scratch, Bea channels her inner lyrical world into lived experience that is fuller and brighter.

events.title: Keira Vana
events.description: Keira Vana is a rising dark-pop artist turning heads with her recent singles Aftertaste and Medicine. Known for sharp, emotional storytelling and a sound that’s both haunting and addictive, she blends confidence and vulnerability into music that stays with you.

events.title: PONS
events.description:
IF YOU STOP YOU DIE - 

Rock n’ Roll will never be a lazy game. PONS is here to set the record straight.

Channeling the wild, untamable spirit of the masters of the road that came before them, PONS brings a relentless, “NO MERCY” approach to DIY touring. Burning more calories in one night than most bands do in a year, PONS doesn’t play just music—they detonate on stage

Taking cues from the anarchic swagger of Iggy Pop and the electronic chaos of Suicide, frontperson Jack Parker spits the digital bile of our decaying, internet-saturated world straight in your face. It’s a new noise pop for the modern age.

With their dashing look and salesman’s eye, PONS has supported notable acts such as Gogol Bordello, Lambrini Girls, A Place To Bury Strangers, Laura Jane Grace, Geese, Vundabar, Frankie and the Witch Fingers, and more. 

BEAR WITNESS TO PONS.

events.title: E.M.E
events.description:
According to his mother, when E.M.E. (born Emmanuel Nwaneto) was baptized, the presiding reverend declared that the child would be a star. Two decades later, he's now fulfilling the reverend's prophecy as an up-and-coming Afrofusion artist based in Denver, Colorado. With over 1.5 million views on his videos and 2 million streams on Spotify and Apple Music, E.M.E is rapidly rising to meet his goal of bringing Afrobeats from Nigeria, to Colorado, and now to the world.

E.M.E returned to music, recording and releasing a few hip-hop tracks. But it wasn't until he linked up with producers Mic Coats and F.L., of the legendary Denver-based label Hitsville. The trio immediately connected and got to work churning out music, ending up with a vault of over sixty songs in just a year. Several were dropped as experimental singles, like "Drago," "Yey Yey,""Love Me Again", "One Day", and "Kolo", as a way to test the waters and dial in E.M.E's sound. "Got Me," his collaboration with Denver R&B royalty Danae Simone, was one of KS107.5's most played songs of 2024. His singles also started charting in Nigeria, climbing to Number 10 on the country's charts for all music genres.

events.title: AKA BK
events.description:
AKA BK is an alternative indie project based in Los Angeles. With influences from bands like The Pixies, The Yeah Yeah Yeahs, and the Breeders, their live show plays like nerves exposed: charged, joyful and disarmingly human, turning their vulnerability into sharpened momentum. The band closes the distance between their fans, both literally and figuratively, inviting them to join in on their tongue-in-cheek moments of mushy playfulness and feverish moshing. 

The foundation of AKA BK is built on long standing friendships, with BK (lead vocals) and Cecile Herledan (bassist) forming their first band at the age of 11 in Metro Detroit. The band is rounded out by fellow guitarists Julian Cullars and Sean Gunner Lee, who have been playing in LA bands since 2013.

events.title: Chuck Prophet and His Cumbia Shoes
events.description:
Chuck Prophet’s streak of more than a dozen critically acclaimed solo records stretches all the way back to 1990, when the California native first shifted focus from his tenure with pioneering neo-psych band Green on Red to working under his own name. Since then, his songs have appeared in a slew of films and television shows, and his work has been covered by Bruce Springsteen, Solomon Burke, Heart, and a host of others. Rolling Stone dubbed him a “streetwise city kid with an eye for the country,” while Uncut proclaimed him a “renaissance-rocker,” and NPR declared that “no one can turn tales from the outer limits into catchy songs quite like Prophet does.” 

Wake The Dead, Chuck Prophet’s extraordinary new album recorded with ¿Qiensave?, dives headfirst into the world of Cumbia music. The songs are intoxicatingly rhythmic, all but demanding you move your body while you listen. There are flashes of rock and roll, punk, surf, and soul, wrapped up in the rich legacy of a genre that traces its roots back hundreds of years and thousands of miles.

speakers.name: Chuck Prophet and His Cumbia Shoes

events.title: Commercial Breaks
events.description: Tight, catchy, succinct, and loud are the best words for Commercial Breaks. Formed in 2025 by a gaggle of rockers and co-conspirators, the group features Lucas Martins, Trey Gutierrez and David Rawlinson, all of whom back Gus Baldwin as “The Sketch” as well as Doran Rawlinson, former drummer of Nolan Potter’s Nightmare Band. The members have performed around Austin for many years but never in such a hook-driven, song-forward capacity. Their debut record out Q4 2025 was recorded entirely at home to cassette tape to ensure absolute commercial viability, and their live shows pursue the title of either Austin’s “Loudest Pop Group” or “Pop-est Loud Group”.

events.title: Differentchris
events.description:
Differentchris is a first generation born and raised Houston based indie artist. His music balances vulnerability and confidence, pairing catchy melodies with introspective themes that explore identity, relationships, and personal growth.

At 11 years old he began gravitating to songwriting and poetry, and knew he wanted to make music. Chris grew up listening to rock and roll with his mother and classic Norteńo with his dad, and fell in love with the structuring of songs.

Known for his dynamic live performances, Differentchris has been rapidly building momentum across Texas, headlining his own regional tour and cultivating a growing fanbase through both recorded releases and high energy shows. His sound sits at the intersection of indie, alternative pop, and modern singer-songwriter music, drawing listeners in with honest storytelling and memorable hooks.

With a clear artistic vision and a strong connection to his audience, Differentchris represents the next wave of Texas artists pushing indie pop forward. His SXSW performance marks a key moment in a fast-growing career rooted in authenticity, consistency, and creative evolution that he envisioned at a young age.

events.title: The Oldest Person in the World
events.description: "The Oldest Person in the World" is a decade-long global journey that chronicles the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate, and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

events.title: Poetic License
events.description: "Poetic License" follows Liz a former therapist and soon-to-be empty nester, who relocates to a new town for her husband’s job – a place where she doesn’t know a soul. Her quiet attempt to settle in takes an unexpected turn when she becomes the point of tension between two inseparable best friends and college seniors, Sam and Ari. As their fierce competition for her attention threatens to upend their lives, Liz is pulled into a tangle of longing, self-discovery, and the intoxicating thrill of being truly seen – forcing her to confront the life she’s built and the one she still craves.

events.title: promqueen
events.description: promqueen is a queer second generation Vietnamese American Pop/Rap Artist based in Austin. Signed under mHart - Texas’ first and only Asian American music label - promqueen operates between Music, Storytelling, Community, and Identity, combining both Vietnamese and English lyrics in her songs and visuals. 2026 will feature the release of her third album, “szn three,” as well as the inaugural MODERN event: a music and fashion festival celebrating Vietnamese American lifestyle taking place in Austin in August.

events.title: Prowess The Testament
events.description:
Hailing from Washington, D.C., Prowess The Testament is a commanding force in hip-hop, blending intricate storytelling, spiritual depth, and masterful lyricism into a singular artistic voice. With a career rooted in authenticity, she has shared stages with Wu-Tang Clan, Jay Electronica, Citizen Cope, Skyzoo, and Sufjan Stevens. Her moniker, bestowed by elder statesman KRS-One after a standout performance during Hip Hop Appreciation Week, reflects her exceptional dedication to craft and culture.

Named a breakout artist to watch by Pitchfork, Prowess is known for immersive, narrative-driven performances that feel part concert, part ritual. Following the Sailor Moon coded Lunar Prelude: Sailor Overture and Legend of the Moon (Deluxe Edition), she is readying Sacred Water, a Dragon Ball Z inspired collaboration with Tsoh Tso, and Royal Flush Chronicles, a three-part series centered on Princess Peach, arriving in 2026.

A best-selling co-author, co-writer of the 2026 Rap Laureate Journal, and host of Boom Bap Chat, Prowess is also an ultra high net worth strategist and real-life alchemist, transforming purpose into art, vision into legacy, and performance into experience.

events.title: Stare Away
events.description: Emerging from the heart of New York City’s underground music scene, Stare Away is the brainchild of Ben Nelson, a project that fuses post-punk intensity with a retro-coded aesthetic inspired by the dark alternative icons of the 1980s. Haunting melodies and brooding soundscapes channel the spirit of goth-driven acts from that era, offering a sonic journey steeped in existential reflection and melancholic beauty. A true embodiment of modern dark romanticism, Stare Away continues to captivate audiences seeking meaning in the shadows.

events.title: Stockz
events.description:
Stockz is a Houston-based artist and entrepreneur redefining what modern hip-hop can represent. Operating at the intersection of music, finance, and education, he transforms real-world experiences—risk, discipline, ownership, and long-term vision—into sharp, motivational records that resonate both on stage and off.

Known for confident delivery and polished, cinematic production, Stockz has performed on major stages including Rolling Loud (U.S. & Thailand), REVOLT World, and a Live Nation–headlined show at House of Blues Houston. He has also brought his sound to academic and cultural spaces, performing at UT Austin’s Student Founder Fest and opening for national tours alongside artists from TDE and the West Coast hip-hop circuit. His live shows blend high energy with intention—equal parts performance and mindset.

Beyond music, Stockz has collaborated with brands such as Nike, adidas, Experian, Samsung, True Religion, and REVOLT TV, bridging corporate partnerships with authentic cultural storytelling. A former Roc Nation–affiliated artist, he brings a rare combination of industry polish, independence, and entrepreneurial clarity to every release.

events.title: Fifteen
events.description: Set in Mexico City, Fifteen reimagines the iconic quinceañera as a chaotic mix of comedy and creature horror. Through Mayte and Ligia’s unbreakable bond, the film explores class divides, the illusions of adolescence, and the fear of growing up—wrapped in kitsch aesthetics, blood-soaked humor, and biting social critique.

events.title: Imposters
events.description: After a couple’s baby boy is taken, the desperate mother learns of a way to bring him back. However, her husband begins to suspect that what she returned with isn't their son.

events.title: Jaylon Ashaun
events.description: Jaylon Ashaun is a nomad redefining connection through music. Blending soulful R&B, hip-hop, and pop with heartfelt lyricism, he creates records that feel both intimate and expansive. His music isn’t just something you hear, it’s something you experience. Each release captures a chapter of his evolving journey, inviting listeners into honest conversations about love, identity, growth, and belonging.

events.title: Morgan Munroe
events.description:
"A voice that stops you in your tracks" – BBC Radio 1

Hailing from Leicester, UK, Morgan Munroe is one of the most exciting voices in contemporary R&B.

Fresh off four standout sets at Glastonbury 2025 and recent performances at SXSW London and SXSW Texas, this award-winning powerhouse continues to push boundaries. She’s earned a BBC Radio 1 Track of the Week, featured on Ghetts’ latest album, and received recognition from Vogue Italia, Mahalia, and DJ Ace. With over 33K monthly listeners on Spotify, her music has landed on the FIFA 2020 soundtrack and gained support from some of the industry's most respected tastemakers.

As part of the MOBO Unsung Class of 2025, Morgan Munroe is showing the world exactly why she’s one to watch - on stage, on record, and beyond.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth

events.title: Pat G
events.description:
Pat G is an American rapper based in Austin, Texas, bringing a refreshing, purpose-driven voice to modern hip-hop. Known for his infectious energy and uplifting message, he creates family-friendly music that still hits hard—blending motivation, faith, and elite lyricism into every performance.

Pat G has performed across California, Florida, Oregon, Texas, Louisiana, and internationally in Toronto, building a growing national and global fanbase. He has been booked three times for the iconic Pecan Street Festival, selected as an official show artist five times, and has performed at major events and venues including Circuit of the Americas, Temple Bloomin’ Festival, and Indie Week Toronto. Closing out 2024, he opened for Lupe Fiasco on four live shows—marking a major career milestone.

Since his first mixtape The Demo (2013), Pat G has continued to evolve through projects including A Different Perspective (2015), The In Between EP (2016), Whatever It Takes (2019), and Talk To Me Nice EP (2024).

Originally from Temple, Texas, Pat G uses music—grounded in his Christian faith—to tell real stories, unite audiences, and inspire hope.

“Be relentless! We don’t just talk it, we live it.”

events.title: Elijah Johnston
events.description:
Atlanta based musician, Elijah Johnston, will release a brand new album, Stupid Soul, via Strolling Bones Records on June 20, 2025. 

Stupid Soul is either Elijah Johnston’s 4th record or his 7th, depending on who you ask, but possibly the first you’ve heard. The logical next step in a career of slow burns, Stupid Soul is neither a record of morose self-reflection nor a frenetic series of genre experiments, settling into a comfortable steady pace: a record built to fit like a glove.

Performed by a small team including Johnston’s brother, manager, and long-time producer, the record is full of small wonders and live band energy, the sound of four close-knit collaborators in pursuit of something timeless. 12-string acoustic guitars, vintage synthesizers, and a relentless belief in the guitar solo round out Johnston’s usual pop rock palate, and the team manages to make a coherent picture out of a mood board that takes just as many cues from Brian Wilson as it does from The Legend of Zelda. 

Elijah began his career in the legendary musical community of Athens, and he was the winner of that city’s 2022 Vic Chesnutt Songwriter of the Year Award. Since then, he has toured nationally and shared stages with acts like Noah Gundersen, Susto, and Elf Power, establishing a name as a recognized songwriter with a potent live show to match.

events.title: Mark Cooper
events.description: Mark Cooper is a multi-disciplinary Rapper and Producer, carrying the torch of Nerdcore from Detroit, Michigan. His branded work consists of a large body of verses and cyphers touching on all things considered “Nerdy” or from Gaming Culture, including references from but not limited to Gaming Systems of all brands, Transformers, Power Rangers, Halo, Naruto, and Tron, earning the perfect branding of “nostalgic.”

events.title: Phoenix Jones: The Rise and Fall of a Real Life Superhero
events.description: In 2010, reports began surfacing of a masked vigilante in a black-and-gold supersuit stopping crime on the streets of Seattle. His name is Phoenix Jones. Armed with pepper spray, a taser, and a team of costumed crime fighters, he quickly becomes an international media sensation. But when his true identity is exposed by the Seattle Police, the heroic image begins to unravel and his team abandons him. Ten years later, as protesters seize six blocks of Seattle and declare a no cop zone, Phoenix reemerges amid legal trouble and public skepticism. Is he a hero, or a con-artist hiding behind a mask?

events.title: Stages
events.description: It's make or break time for Ben Garza as he embarks on his solo first tour after the collapse of his band. By his side are Rita, his former tour manager stepping away from her stable life to help him, and Parker, a remaining bandmate who joins Ben as a utility player. However, Rita also secures Jessie Ramos as the opening act, a rising star whose sudden surge in popularity will completely destabilize Ben. Throughout this musical odyssey, Ben will face characters on the road who challenge his ideas of success, relevance, and purpose. Some encounters offer hope; others deepen his doubt. By the tour’s end, Ben must decide whether to keep chasing the life he once had—or chart a new path forward.
events.venue: Rollins Theatre at the Long Center

events.title: They Will Kill You
events.description: "They Will Kill You" unleashes a blood-soaked, high-octane horror-action-comedy in which a young woman must survive the night at the Virgil, a demonic cult's mysterious and twisted death-trap of a lair, before becoming their next offering in a uniquely brazen, big screen battle of epic kills and wickedly dark humor.

events.title: The Tullamarines
events.description:
The amalgamation of four distinct voices from Adelaide, The Tullamarines tell their stories through a shared perspective that feels intimate, honest, and quietly uplifting. Josh, Angus, Benny and Lucinda met on the local gig circuit, quickly bonding over a mutual love of songwriting and collaboration. From those early connections, they’ve crafted a sound that reflects each member’s individual sensibilities - a style they affectionately call cosy-pop.
 
Their songs move through life’s highs and lows with the warmth of an old friend, inviting listeners into their living room, putting the kettle on, and sitting with whatever feeling the day brings. That sense of closeness runs through both their recorded work and their live shows.
 
Having appeared on festival line-ups including Beyond The Valley, Laneway Festival, Spin Off Festival and New Year’s Eve on the Hill, and toured extensively alongside artists such as Old Mervs, The Preatures, Ball Park Music and Alex Lahey, The Tullamarines continue to build a reputation for heartfelt songwriting and deeply human performances.

events.title: Buzz Screening 3
events.description: A film that everyone is talking about, and audiences need another chance to see it.

events.title: The Sun Never Sets
events.description:
Wendy's life is thrown into chaos when her boyfriend, Jack, who is older and divorced with children, insists they take space to evaluate the relationship. During their break, Wendy unexpectedly runs into her ex, Chuck, forcing the three of them into a confusing and volatile triangle.

The film was shot on 35mm on location in Alaska.

events.title: Shai Gabriel
events.description: An artist at the crossroads of country and hip-hop, Shai Gabriel creates the kind of songs that feel as epic as a movie: gripping, unpredictable, immense in scope but rooted in raw emotion. On his journey, the Texas-bred singer/songwriter charts a cinematic road trip through the wilds of the American South, bringing a powerful new depth to his storytelling while pushing further into the country/folk-inspired sound he's explored in recent years. Drawing inspirations from Country, Pop, Hip Hop and Gospel he creates a dynamic sound that captures the hearts of fans.

events.title: American Dollhouse
events.description: A woman inherits her childhood home, seeking solace from a chaotic city life marked by addiction and debt. Unbeknownst to her, a psychotic neighbor becomes disturbingly obsessed with her due to a haunting resemblance to the neighbor’s deceased mother. As the fixation turns violent, her friends begin disappearing one by one, drawing her into a perverted, blood-soaked Christmas nightmare she may not survive.

events.title: Buzz Screening 4
events.description: A film that everyone is talking about, and audiences need another chance to see it.

events.title: CAZAYOUX
events.description:
Swamp funk. Psychedelic soul.
Global rhythms + deep improvisation

In April 2026, the band releases Alpha Centauri, produced by Nico Léophonte in Austin, a record centered on ignition, growth, and the shared journey of the band as artists

Aboubacar Sylla — Djembe/Congas, Balafon
Alex Freeman — Bass
Damien Valenzuela — Tenor Saxophone
Forest Cazayoux — Drums
Fumihito Sugawara — Guitar
Joe Woullard — Baritone Saxophone, Flute
Patrick Harwell — Trombone
Tate Christian — Hammond Organ, Keys, Vocals

events.title: Foliage
events.description:
The Inland Empire can either suffocate you or make you work even harder. For the past 10 years, Manuel Joseph Walker’s prolific output as Foliage has helped him become a widely recognized figurehead in modern Shoegaze. A chameleonic producer, Walker draws from the broader palettes of Post-Punk while slyly incorporating textures and ideas from Hip-Hop and Electronic records, revealing ephemeral but lasting impressions that feel simultaneously intimate and ritualistic, something you can listen to in your headphones late at night or shout along with a cold lager in your hand. His song “It’s Time” has been featured in nearly 19K TikToks from brands such as Le Creuset, F1, & Netflix.

With his latest single “Missing Hearts”, featuring a music video he directed, Walker has produced his most arena-ready tune yet. With millions of streams and a reputation for unforgettable live performances, Foliage has evolved from best-kept secret to cornerstone of Indie's next generation of hitmakers. In the wake of their first full-length record in six years on the way, Foliage is poised to make a massive splash at this year’s SXSW and all through 2026.

events.title: Future Nobodies
events.description:
Future Nobodies is a genre-bending trio from Chicago, IL. Influenced by the 2000’s NYC indie scene as well as 1980’s post-punk and new wave, the band has developed a nostalgic,  emotionally charged sound that is solely their own. Often described as “sad happy music to dance to,” the trio croon like Morrissey over bass heavy melodies and crying guitar licks.
The band released their first album in 2021 (Hotel Del La Muerte) as an online project that gained immediate traction. In 2022 they released their Over it/Apasionada EP. “Over It” was placed on an official Spotify playlist causing the song to reach over a million streams and gain the band over 50K monthly listeners overnight. In 2023 they performed at Riot Fest. The line up included acts such as Death Cab For Cutie, Queens of the Stoneage, and The Cure. In 2024 they released their self-titled sophomore album, Future Nobodies. The album was picked up and distributed by Young & Cold Records. With the record labels help, the band made their European debut at Germany’s annual Wave Gotik Treffen Festival. Since then, the band has gained underground popularity and is currently touring cities across the U.S.

events.title: Keetheweeb
events.description:
Meet Keetheweeb: A Rising Star in Music and Gaming

Keetheweeb is an anonymous female singer known for her eclectic blend of genres, including Pop, Cinematic, and Nerdcore. Hailing from Louisiana, she burst onto the scene with her unique sound, captivating audiences with heartfelt lyrics and infectious melodies. She is widely known for her anime inspired tracks like “Mastermind” (Ayanokoji) and “Bomb” (Reze).

Her notable collaborations include working with renowned artists like Rustage on the hit track “Assimilate” which showcased their complementary styles. She also teamed up with Johnald to make “Breakdown” for their twist on a K Pop Demon Hunters Fan Song that gained traction on YouTube .

In the gaming world, Keetheweeb has made waves with placements in popular gaming competitions such as EVO, where her track “Waves” became a fan favorite. She has contributed thematic music to Genshin Impact, enhancing player experience with her signature sound.

With a growing fanbase and a flair for innovation, Keetheweeb is poised to become a major player in both the music and gaming industries. Keep an eye on this talented artist as she continues to break boundaries and redefine her craft!

events.title: Mae Muller
events.description:
Mae Muller is one of Britain’s most dynamic and boundary-pushing pop artists. With a voice forged through honesty and raw emotion, Mae has become an authentic voice for a generation, fearless in her vulnerability, unapologetic in her expression, and unafraid to tell it like it is. 

Mae’s shows are more than just live performances, they are moments of connection. She writes songs that dive into real relationships, self-worth, heartbreak, empowerment, and resilience. Her lyrics and performances have drawn praise for their relatability and emotional truth.

Having already toured arenas with major acts, headlined her own tours, performed on international festival bills, and represented her country on one of music’s largest stages, the journey is only just beginning. With her debut album out and her fanbase ever growing, Mae is ready to build on her momentum, embodying an artist who is fearless, authentic, and endlessly evolving.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth Patio

events.title: Magic Rockers of Texas
events.description: Magic Rockers of Texas are a punchy power-pop rock band from Austin, TX, delivering gritty hooks and high-energy live shows rooted in catchy songwriting and garage-infused rock & roll. Led by charismatic singer Jim Campo, the group features Will Grover on guitar, Chris Kues on guitar & synth, Pat Ford on bass, and McGarrity Stanley on drums. Since forming in the mid-2010s, they’ve become local favorites, known for infectious riffs, spirited performances across Austin’s venues, and releases like the album Gorging on American Fare and singles such as “Houston” and "Words in a Bin." Blending melodic pop sensibilities with raw, fast-paced rock, Magic Rockers of Texas embody the vibrant independent music spirit of their hometown.

events.title: Rock Springs
events.description: A grieving Chinese and Vietnamese American family move to an isolated house in a new town. Eight-year-old Gracie, silent since the death of her beloved father, begins to interact with a dark presence in the woods behind their new home. Her mother, Emily, struggles to hide her suffocating grief, cutting her off from Gracie and her mother-in-law, Nai Nai. When Gracie is taken by the dark presence, her family has to confront the ghosts of the past and their shared trauma to find her. The story intertwines historical events from the 1885 massacre of Chinese coal miners with present-day supernatural elements, culminating in a poignant exploration of loss, memory, and reconciliation with the past.

events.title: Social Cig
events.description:
Born & brewed in Wisconsin, Social Cig is the 'Indie-Skate-Rock' music project of Filipino American, Parker Schultz. Consisting of contagious authenticity, cheery live shows, and cultivating an original story with an attitude of gratitude, Social Cig is creating full-circle moments. Leafing through global music scenes with an ambitious DIY approach and writing songs that capture a genuine outlook from a modern-day Midwest cowboy, Social Cig has become a well-rounded grassroots venture.

A Social Cig song sorts the extraordinaries of personhood; a lyrical short story woven together with playful strength and catchy grips in the feel-good realm of indie rock. Sketching a memoir and gardening an actively verdant fan base, Social Cig continues to expand its landscape by sharing the stage with acts such as Wet Leg, Lime Cordiale, Noah Kahan, CAKE, Motherfolk, PREP, Arlo Parks, M.A.G.S., Kainalu, Ax and the Hatchetmen, Miloe, The Symposium, Dizzy, The Crowe Boys, Landon Conrath, Motel Breakfast, Windser, Michael Cera Palin, and Lowertown.

events.title: IYLA
events.description: Iyla is a Los Angeles-based singer-songwriter who blends soul, jazz, r&b, and pop into her music. Her stage name, which means "moonlight", reflects her night owl tendencies and ends in "L.A.", a nod to her hometown.

events.title: Bagworm
events.description:
Carroll’s worldview is dominated by the threat of catastrophe and the decline of morality in the face of human extinction. Then he steps on a rusty nail. He stumbles through the modern world, searching for romance, shedding toxic friendships, and fighting for truth... all while struggling to maintain his deteriorating health and sanity. 

As his moral crusade edges closer to self-destruction, Carroll is confronted with the ultimate existential question: are we really doomed, or is he just dying of tetanus?

events.title: Forbidden Fruits
events.description: At a mall store, Apple leads a secret witch cult with coworkers Cherry and Fig. New hire Pumpkin questions their sisterhood, forcing them to confront inner darkness or meet violent ends.

events.title: Hot Garbage
events.description: Hot Garbage melt into a heavily volatile yet undeniably palatable amalgamation of sonic elements. Calling on the driving rhythms of dark post-punk and motorik krautrock, the Toronto-based outfit seamlessly works shining melodies and swirling textures into deliberate, brooding arrangements. Since forming in 2015, the four-piece have toured extensively throughout Canada, the United States, Europe and the United Kingdom, bringing their intense live sets to festivals such as Levitation, Freakout Fest, Treefort, SXSW, Sled Island, FME, M for Montreal and Pop Montreal, and sharing the stage with notable acts such as Osees, Ty Segall, L.A. Witch, Frankie and the Witch Fingers, JJUUJJUU, Mdou Moctar, Wand and Kikagaku Moyo. The quartet recently returned with Precious Dream (January 19, 2024 via Mothland & Exag’ Records), a sprawling collection of songs written in isolation and brought together alongside visionary producer Graham Walsh (METZ, Preoccupations, Holy Fuck, !!!), offering an exhilarating new breath into the world of post-punk and modern psychedelia, a listening experience that is equally cathartic and introspective.

events.title: Wim Tapley & The Cannons
events.description:
Based in Athens, Georgia, Wim Tapley came of age playing venues in Washington D.C. and its sprawling suburbs. There, he honed his voice with the passion of a born troubadour, drawing in a diverse fanbase with his easy showmanship and distinct style.
 
Since 2021, Athens has been home to Wim and his live band The Cannons. His first week in town, Wim made his way onto a local bill, etching a name for himself as a fresh and favorite hometown voice. He is ardently received by his ever-growing following at legendary regional venues like the 9:30 Club, Eddie’s Attic, and the Georgia Theatre—the latter of which he’s sold out more than once—and on tours across the country.
 
Firmly rooted in Americana and dashed with glamorous pop sensibilities, the swinging depths of neo-soul, and a sprinkling of riotous horns, Wim’s arresting sound is as fresh as it is ageless, as fevered as it is raucous fun. 
 
A sonic westward expansion of fuzzed-out guitars, defiant horns, and dusty vocals, his discography blazes a fresh new take on folk-pop while honoring the songwriting giants that paved the way before him like Jason Isbell, Bill Withers, and Chris Stapleton.

events.title: Grocery Bag
events.description: Grocery Bag are the latest in a new breed of face-melting rock & roll straight out of Austin, Texas. The garage rock-psych-punk 4 piece, led by diminutive singer Bella Martinez, have been tearing up stages around Texas since 2023, being handpicked by the likes of Osees, Frankie & The Witch Fingers & Farmer's Wife to support on multiple shows as well as a critically-acclaimed set at Levitation Festival 2024. Following this breakthrough performance, the band were added as main support on Psychedelic Porn Crumpets tour in April/May 2025, playing 22 shows & solidifying their reputation as one of the best live bands in the country. Their debut album 'Break You' (released in Nov 2023) is a great raw snapshot of young talented musicians creating something exciting, to-the-point, that leaves you replaying time & time again. New music is expected early 2026!

events.title: Anton The Artist
events.description:
Anton The Artist is a rising independent recording artist known for his dynamic versatility, polished delivery, and undeniable stage presence. Blending melodic flows with sharp lyricism, Anton creates music that bridges raw authenticity with mainstream appeal. His sound pulls from hip-hop, R&B influences, and contemporary trap elements, allowing him to craft records that feel both personal and high-energy.

With a growing catalog and consistent live performances, Anton has built a reputation for commanding the stage and connecting directly with audiences. His music reflects real-life experiences, ambition, resilience, and the grind of an artist determined to level up. Focused on longevity over moments, Anton The Artist continues to expand his brand, refine his sound, and solidify his place as one of the next independent talents to watch

events.title: Jakeneutron
events.description:
Jakeneutron is a black multimedia animator and Nerdcore artist from Central Florida! He is also the founder and director of Team Neutron!
Him and his Team are behind fan animated music videos such as “Don’t Listen”, “Play My Way” & “Jax Toy”! Many of their projects crossover into fandoms from all over, whether they’re cartoons or indie games! It’s whatever they’re all passionate about!

events.title: Trophy Wife
events.description: Trophy Wife is unapologetic. Based in Brooklyn, this trio bares all through a hazy, distorted lens. With the 2024 release of their debut album Get Ugly, McKenzie Iazzetta’s confessional lyrics, Christian Pace’s riff-like bass lines, and Michael Martelli’s pounding drums transform raw diary entries into cathartic anthems for the parts of ourselves that are best swept under the rug.

events.title: CQ Wrestling
events.description:
CQ Wrestling are a British grunge band led by best friends and songwriters Charlie Woods and Jake Mac, delivering a fierce yet melodic 90s-inspired sound. Their lyrics tackle social and political unrest while offering moments of euphoric escape, and their chaotic, high-energy shows have built a devoted following through three sold-out UK tours, Glastonbury 2025, and European festival appearances.

After earning critical acclaim for their debut album Plus Ultra (EMI, 2023) with support from BBC Radio 1, 6 Music, and Radio X, the band are now fully independent, embracing complete creative freedom. Their first independent single, Catherine Wheels, hit the cover of Spotify’s Rock List, and their upcoming release, Guns In Their Hands, is a defiant rallying cry about choice, resilience, and connection amid the chaos of the world.
events.venue: British Music Embassy @ Palm Door on Sixth

events.title: Nikki Gold
events.description:
Nashville-based singer-songwriter Nikki Gold grew up half country, half city—riding horses one day, chasing urban rhythms the next—and has lived across the U.S. and the UK. Her voice, part modern Joni Mitchell with a subtle Celtic bend, cuts with honesty that resonates.

With years helping people navigate pain, transformation, and life’s messy edges, Nikki turns love, dating, and self-discovery into songs that stick, sting, and uplift—all with a wink of humor. Produced by John D. Willis (Taylor Swift, Kenny Chesney, Shania Twain), her upcoming EP Maverick—with its title single released in February 2026—captures the electric space between who you were and who you’re becoming.

Through her “2nd VERSE” series and live shows, Nikki creates music that grabs, shakes, and inspires—a soundtrack for the next chapter

events.title: Odanga
events.description:
Odanga is an Afrofusion artist, battle rapper, producer, and engineer blending African tradition with American hip-hop. His sound fuses soulful R&B, sharp lyricism, and vibrant Afro rhythms into a cinematic, emotionally grounded experience.

With over 15 years on the mic, Odanga has performed from freestyle cyphers to major stages, including Sway In The Morning at SXSW 2018.
